title: fix(multiaxis): start and exit picks for the multi-axis contour
body:
## What changed

The Multi-Axis Contour (`OpType::MultiAxisContour`, the drive-curve planner `multiaxis::contour_curve`) takes a start point and an exit point. This is slice 2 of #3330. Slice 1 (the 5-Axis Contour) is PR #4006.

The title uses `fix`: the issue has the `bug` label, and PR #4028 used `fix` for the same reason.

Behaviour (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve_seam.rs`, hook in `contour_curve_seamed`):

- Each pick acts on the drive curve nearest it. The other curves keep their automatic cut. The cut order of the curves does not change.
- A pick with a Z is read in 3D. A pick without a Z is read in XY.
- Closed curve, start: the curve starts at its point nearest the pick. A foot between two vertices becomes a new vertex on that segment.
- Closed curve, exit: the curve cuts its full lap from its seam. Then it runs on along its own points to its point nearest the exit pick, and the tool leaves there.
- Open curve: the start pick selects the end where the cut starts (the nearer end). The exit pick selects the end where the cut leaves. The direction of the curve can reverse.
- The re-sequence occurs before the walk. Thus the rest law, the tilt limit (`command_axis` in the max-tilt cone) and the shank dodge judge each station of the picked path, as on the automatic path. The app's centre-cut audit (`audit_posed`) and the verify pass also read the picked path.
- The kind has no leads, so there is no lead-room law.
- With no pick, `apply` returns before it touches the curves. The path is byte-identical.
- `PickCapability::Ring` for the kind. The MCP `edit_operation` schema says how the kind reads a pick.

## Refusals (by name, before any motion)

- `start point (x, y): the nearest drive curve stands D mm away, farther than R mm (1.5 tool diameters) - ...` (also for the exit).
- `start point (...): drive curve N is open and its cut can start only at an end; its nearest end (...) stands D mm away, farther than R mm - ...` (also for the exit: `leave only at an end`).
- `exit point (...): it is nearer the end of open drive curve N where the start point begins the cut - ...`.
- `start point (...): the plunge column over drive curve N at (x, y, z) crosses the part - ...` and `exit point (...): the retract column over drive curve N at (...) crosses the part - ...`. The column law sweeps the ball up the vertical line to the hop plane, every 0.25 mm, and it checks the shank at each step when shank avoidance is on.

## Mutations

Each mutation was applied alone, the pins were run, and the source was restored.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `curve_seam::rotate` keeps the automatic seam (start seat off) | RED: `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M2 | `run_on`: the full lap dropped (the exit becomes a chord) | RED: `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick` |
| M3 | the plunge column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | the retract column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | open curve: the start reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`; app: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| M6 | open curve: the exit reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends` |
| M7 | the same-end exit refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M8 | the open start end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M9 | the open exit end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M10 | the curve reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M11 | the column sweep reads only the station (no samples up the column) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| A1 | the app arm passes an empty seam | RED: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| A3 | the kind's capability back to `PICK_OWED` | RED: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick`, `multiaxis_contour_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` |

## Readings

- The pins that say "the cut geometry does not change" sample each cut move every 0.25 mm in both directions. Each sample of the picked path must be within 0.02 mm of the automatic ball-centre path (no chord, no gouge). Each sample of the automatic path must be within 0.02 mm of the picked path (no part of the curve left uncut). The walk's chord budget is 0.0025 mm.
- Box 40 x 40 x 15, ring at z = 7.5, ball r = 3: the start pick (20, -1) gives a first ball centre at (20.0, -3.0, 7.5) within 0.05 mm. The exit pick (-1, 20) gives a last ball centre at (-3.0, 20.0, 7.5).
- A canopy slab at z 18 to 20 above the middle of the y = 0 wall: a pick under it is refused for the plunge and for the retract. A pick on the x = 0 wall cuts.

## Pinning tests

- motion `multiaxis` (module `curve_seam`): `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_without_a_pick_is_the_automatic_path_byte_for_byte`.
- app `start_exit_shared` (module `multiaxis_contour`): `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name`, `multiaxis_contour_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `undo`, `redo`); and `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated).
- No new top-level test binary: the new files are modules of `multiaxis` and `start_exit_shared`.

## Goldens moved

None expected. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- A pick on a shank-avoid path where the shank, not the ball, blocks the column. The shank step uses the existing `shank_hits_at`; no pin drives it.
- A closed drive curve through the application (the app pins use the box's four open top edges). The closed curve is pinned at motion scale.
- A setup with a rotated frame: the picks and the drive curves are both in the setup frame, as for the 5-Axis Contour.

## Code shape

- `curve.rs` had 860 lines. Its unit tests moved, unchanged, to `curve_tests.rs`. It now has 719 lines, with the hook. A further split is a follow-up.
- No new crate edge.

## Remaining kinds of #3330

Parallel5D, Swarf, AdvancedSwarf, RotaryContour, RotaryParallel, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Flow5D.

## Gate

All on head `8d61b24d9` (local Mac):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 216 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: multiaxis`, `motion suites: pivot5d`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.4 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy step: none (P2).

Decision: `docs/decisions/3330-multiaxis-contour-picks.md`.

Effort: max.

Changelog: The Multi-Axis Contour takes a start point and an exit point: each pick re-sequences the drive curve nearest it, and an impossible pick is refused by name.

Refs #3330

title: fix(mcp): release the ui link owner lock by unlock, not by a close
body:
## Cause

The post-merge gate of `3bb6647f6` failed in `mcp_live`, test `ui_link_owner::a_false_server_that_proves_the_token_gets_no_tool_call_when_the_window_has_ended`. The cause is a race between a lock release by a close and a concurrent child process start. Part of it is in the product code of #3995 (PR #4020), and not only in the test.

- On Unix, a `flock` belongs to the open file, not to the descriptor.
- When a thread starts a child process (`Command::spawn`), the child holds a copy of each descriptor until its `exec` closes it.
- A close of the lock file during that time does not release the lock.
- `mcp_live` runs many tests in parallel, and some of them start `camcraft-cli` children. Thus the race occurs often in that binary.

The two places:

1. **Product code**: `link_owner::owner`. To prove that a window has ended, it takes the free lock and released it only by the close of the file. When a fork occurred at that moment, the lock stayed held. The next lock test then read the ended window as alive, and the CLI dialed its address. This is the defect class that #3995 closes. In a looped run, the CLI dialed the false server of the crashed-window test (`Busy` after the hello timeout).
2. **Test code**: the tests ended a stand-in window with `drop(lock)`. The CLI's lock test after the hello then saw the lock still held, opened a session and sent the tool call to the false server. The failure text was `Failed("... closed the link before it answered")` at `ui_link_owner.rs:111`.

## What changed

- `link_owner::owner`: after it takes a free lock, it calls `File::unlock` before the close. If the unlock fails, the entry is unproved and is not dialed.
- `Registration::drop` (a window closes): unlocks after it removed its files.
- `link::open`: unlocks on the bind-error path.
- Tests: the new helper `release_lock` ends a stand-in window with an unlock, as the OS does at a process end. Both `ui_link_owner` tests that end a window use it.

No retry, no sleep and no `#[ignore]`. Decision record: `docs/decisions/4041-ui-link-lock-release.md`.

Residual (in the decision record): when a window process crashes while one of its own threads starts a child, the lock stays held until that child runs `exec`. This is a short time, and the OS ends it.

## Readings

Loop: the whole `mcp_live` binary (25 tests), `--test-threads=24` as on the runner, four loops at the same time for load, from `crates/app`:

- Unchanged binary (`origin/main` `3bb6647f6` tree): 150 runs. `a_false_server_that_proves_the_token_gets_no_tool_call_when_the_window_has_ended` failed in 42 runs. `a_crashed_windows_file_is_removed_and_its_port_is_never_dialed` failed in 2 runs. (These runs used a copy of the binary with no `assets/` beside it, so `live_gate_allows_explicitly_approved_calls_and_never_auto_approves_post_or_machine_edits` also failed in all 150. That is an artifact of the copy, not a result.)
- Test fix only (the product code unchanged): 200 runs, 1 failure. `a_crashed_windows_file_is_removed_and_its_port_is_never_dialed` returned `Busy`: the CLI dialed the false server. This showed the product defect in `owner`.
- Final head (the test fix and the product fix): **200 of 200 runs passed**, in place, with no failure in any test.

Gate on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 3 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (app build, app lib, `mcp_live`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Pinning tests: `ui_link_owner::a_false_server_that_proves_the_token_gets_no_tool_call_when_the_window_has_ended` and `ui_link_owner::a_crashed_windows_file_is_removed_and_its_port_is_never_dialed`, pinned by the 200-run loop.
- Light lane: not run. The diff does not reach the light twins (motion adaptive twins and `pocket_pass_start`), and it changes no post and no toolpath. No heavy step: this is a P2 PR.

## Not exercised

- Windows and macOS were not run. On Windows, `LockFileEx` belongs to the handle, and std makes handles non-inheritable. The explicit unlock is correct there too.
- A crash of a real window process during a child start was not emulated (see the residual).

Changelog: none

Fixes #4041

title: docs(process): the Side branch rule for side/path-kernel
body:
## What changed

- `AGENTS.md`: a new rule **Side branch** in "Issue Law", directly after **Overlapping issues stack**. The two rules are about a PR whose base is not `main`, so a reader finds them together. "Pull Request Law" gets only short pointers to the rule.
- `AGENTS.md`: three small edits remove contradictions with the new rule:
  - **Start from the latest main**: a new sub-bullet "A sub-PR of a side branch starts from that branch (**Side branch**)."
  - **Done on a branch**: a new sentence "A sub-PR of a side branch uses `--base side/<name>` and `Refs #N`, and its issue keeps `in-review` after the merge (**Side branch**)."
  - **When PRs merge**: a new sentence "Never use `--delete-branch` on a PR whose head is a side branch."
  - **When a PR merges**: a new sentence "A sub-PR of a side branch is the exception (**Side branch**)."
- `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md`: step 1 uses `origin/side/path-kernel` for a sub-PR. Step 5 gives the base, the body start line, `Refs #N` and the gate base for a sub-PR.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: the switch-over PR merges only on the maintainer's word and without `--delete-branch`. A sub-PR keeps its `side/*` base (no retarget to `main`). After a sub-PR merge, its issue keeps `in-review` and gets the fixed comment.
- `docs/decisions/4042-side-branch-rule.md`: the decisions of this PR.

## The new rule, in full

```
- **Side branch** (#4023, #4042). A side branch `side/<name>` collects the
  sub-PRs of one large change. Then one PR takes it to `main`. Only the
  maintainer permits a side branch. `side/path-kernel` is the one that
  exists. It is made from `main` after this rule merges. Its plan is in
  `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md`.
  - The branch is protected against a force-push and a deletion. It is
    never rebased. Each change goes to it through a sub-PR.
  - A sub-PR has one issue. Its worktree is made from `origin/side/<name>`,
    on a branch `issue/N-<slug>`. It opens as a draft with `--base
    side/<name>`.
  - The body of a sub-PR starts with `Side branch: side/<name>`. It ends
    with `Refs #N`, not `Fixes #N`: a merge into a side branch closes no
    issue.
  - A sub-PR gets the quick pass and the collaborator review as each other
    PR. It merges with a merge commit when its review is clean, also as a
    `feat`. `--delete-branch` deletes only the sub-PR's own branch.
  - The issue of a merged sub-PR keeps `in-review` until the switch-over PR
    merges. The merging session comments `merged to side/<name> in PR #M;
    closes at the switch-over` on the issue.
  - `main` is merged into the side branch with `git merge`, through a sync
    PR into the side branch. Never rebase, never force-push. Do this after
    each merge batch on `main` that touches the code of the side branch,
    and at least each week. If the two sides changed the same logic, the
    sync stops and the maintainer decides (`resolve-conflicts` skill).
  - The gates are local: `post-merge.yml` covers `main` only. Each sub-PR
    runs its pinning tests, the quick gate of its diff against
    `origin/side/<name>`, the example catalog suites and the light lane.
    The head of the side branch gets one local batch gate after each sync,
    inside the build limit. A red batch is fixed on the side branch before
    the next sub-PR merges.
  - The lane and in-flight limits count a sub-PR as each other PR.
  - The switch-over is one PR from `side/<name>` to `main`. It lists
    `Fixes #N` for each issue that it closes. It merges only on the
    maintainer's word: an agent review is not enough. It merges without
    `--delete-branch`.
```

## Decisions

- Place: in "Issue Law" after **Overlapping issues stack**, not in "Pull Request Law". The reason is above.
- A sub-PR that is a `feat` merges into the side branch when its review is clean. The feat-at-cut rule applies to the switch-over PR to `main`.
- The protection text names only what the maintainer approved: no force-push and no deletion.

## Tests

Docs and process files only. No build and no gate ran: the diff has no code.

Not exercised: the steps on a real `side/path-kernel` branch. The branch does not exist yet; the coordinator makes it after this PR merges.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: medium

Fixes #4042

title: feat(post): Agie Wire EDM posts reentrant line and arc openings
body:
Stacked on #4022. Own commit range: `028530986..bea85a429` (one commit). Retarget this PR to `main` before #4022 merges.

## Behaviour

- A Wire Contour with the side **Die** on one selected closed DXF chain now posts through the Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision) post. Before this change, the post refused it ("reads a selected DXF chain only for a captured punch").
- The ISO keeps the nominal walls. It starts at the seam and runs counter-clockwise, with `G01`, `G02` and `G03` blocks and incremental `I`/`J` centres. A clockwise drawing is reversed.
- The SBL and SBR are the zero-step die setup of #2957 (`c_die`). Only the stem, the stock and the hole change.
- The control makes the lead, the passes and the separation. CamCraft writes no lead.
- The app reads the placed walls with the code of the inspection export (#3219). That code is now shared in `crates/app/src/operation/agie_opening.rs`. The inspection export keeps its behaviour.
- The ordinary Wire Contour generator and the wire laws still judge the generated kerf before the native post runs.
- New: `crates/post/src/agie/opening.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/opening/walls.rs` (exact distances between lines and arcs), `examples/agie/reentrant-die.{dxf,camscript}`, a user guide section and `docs/decisions/3178-agie-reentrant-opening.md`.

## Rules and refusals

Each rule uses the rough offset of the 20 mm QN2 row (0.245 mm). Each refusal names the rule and its values.

| Rule | Refusal starts with | Control evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Joints and arc centres on the 0.00001 mm grid, equal squared radii at both arc ends | `Native arc radius rule` (both radii) | `RADB` (0.001 mm difference): the control moved the centre by half the difference. `RADA` (0.003 mm): no plotted path, no message. |
| An inside fillet of the plate (a CCW arc of the CCW opening) has a radius larger than 0.245 mm | `Native arc offset rule` (radius, offset) | `FILR` (R0.2): FORMALCHECK passed, but the Main pass left the arc out and cut a sharp corner. The control does not refuse it. CamCraft refuses it. |
| An arc joins its neighbours tangentially; only two straight walls meet at a sharp corner | `Native joint rule` (the point) | `REENT20`: the sharp tooth tips got round R0.245 turns. |
| A sharp inside corner of the plate leaves at most 0.002 mm | `Strict cover rule` (angle, rest) | Same law as the polygon die. |
| Walls that are not neighbours are more than 2 × (corner reach + 0.245) apart | `The walls from … are … mm apart` | Conservative bound. |
| Hole inside, more than 1 mm from each wall; straight entry wall parallel to X or Y; 3 mm lead and 3 mm of wall each side; lead 0.4 mm clear of other walls | hole and entry texts | `REENT20`: straight lead from the hole to the seam. |
| 0.4 mm of stock beyond each wall and arc extremum; 20 mm plate | stock texts | Same as the polygon die. |

"Tangent entry radius larger than the offset" does not apply: CamCraft writes no arc lead.

## Imported on an offline copy of the control's software (2026-11-25)

- `REENT20` (unmodified output of `examples/agie/reentrant-die.camscript`):
  - The ISO and SBL arrived byte for byte. The tree showed `CCB030[0]`.
  - One formal error before TECCUT ("Technologie : te definiëren"). TECCUT row 0199 (Dia 0.25, H20, Ra 0.30) was assigned. The tree showed `CCB030[4]`, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.
  - FORMALCHECK: no errors. Only the two usual warnings.
  - Plot: the Main pass runs counter-clockwise 0.245 mm inside the opening. The fillets became concentric arcs of r − 0.245. The clockwise R4 tongue tip became a concentric `G02` of R4.245. The Main pass ends 1 mm before the seam. The trims run reversed.
- `FILR`, `RADA` and `RADB` are the same job with one hand edit of the ISO each. CamCraft refuses those edits.

## Readings

- Golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/REENT20.ISO`, line by line in `opening_tests.rs`. N0001 is the seam (the foot of the 5 mm lead from X0 Y−7). N0003 is the R2 corner. N0005 and N0009 are the tooth fillets. N0006 to N0008 are the tooth. N0013 and N0017 are the tongue fillets. N0015 is the R4 tongue tip (G02 about X0 Y4). N0022 returns to the seam.
- The CAM path of the example: 25 moves, the wire laws clean, one captured slug of 789.12 mm².

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::opening_tests` (9 tests): the golden ISO, the clockwise drawing, the entry choice, each refusal with its values.
- `camcraft-app --test agie_native`:
  - `opening::a_reentrant_line_and_arc_die_posts_g02_g03_and_the_checked_die_setup` (ISO golden, SBL = DIE20 with the stem, stock and hole changed, SBR).
  - `opening::a_small_concave_arc_an_island_or_an_outside_hole_publishes_nothing`.
- `camcraft-app --test wire_dxf_selection`: `arcs::a_reentrant_die_of_lines_and_arcs_passes_the_laws_and_a_2um_gouge_does_not`. The laws accept the generated cut. A 2 µm move of the tongue tip arc into the plate gives a `Gouge`.

## Goldens moved

None. One golden is new: `REENT20.ISO`. The straight-only and arc punch Agie goldens are byte-identical (the whole `agie_native` suite and the post lib `agie::` tests pass).

## Not exercised

- A physical machine and the slug restraint.
- An off-grid DXF (refused), sharp joints at an arc (refused), conical arcs and other heights than 20 mm.

## Gate

All on the head `bea85a429`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the diff of #4022 touches `crates/geometry`, so quick fell back to the batch plan. 1215 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 48.1 min. This includes `agie_native`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `wire_post`, `sodick_wire_post`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `post suites: script_agie_native`, the post lib, the ui suites and `clippy -D warnings`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Strict clippy `-p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- P6: no heavy step.

Changelog: The Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision) post writes a selected die opening from a DXF chain of lines and arcs, also a reentrant one, with native G01/G02/G03 and the zero-step die setup; arcs that the control would change are refused by name.

Process change: yes

Fixes #3178

title: fix(mcp): list every accepted field of a kind in list_operation_types
body:
## What changed

Before this change, `list_operation_types` listed only the fields that the default params serialize. Agents did not find optional fields (pocket `tilt` and `rest`, the plasma `feed` and pierce keys, the Wire Contour extras). Enum fields showed only `"string"`.

- New module `crates/app/src/mcp/kind_fields.rs` with `kind_fields/trace.rs`. The trace runs the `Deserialize` of `ParamsDto` with a recording deserializer. It records the struct field names, the enum variant names and the `Option` fields of each kind. One rule applies to all kinds. The PR adds no hand list of field names.
- Each field row now has these additions:
  - `"optional": true` when the defaults do not write the field.
  - `"values"` for an enum field (for example drill `cycle`, pocket `entry` and `strategy`, wire `side`).
  - `"shape"` for an object or array field (for example `rest`, `tilt`, `tabs`, `links`). A `key?` in the shape is optional.
- Two kinds flatten a struct (`#[serde(flatten)]`): `thread` and `sinker_side_burn`. Serde gives no key names for such a struct. Thus `kind_fields::flattened` traces the flattened type by itself, and it names the six optional keys of the thread variant.
- A second small trace (`kind_fields/written.rs`, a recording serializer) gives the keys that the kind's params can write. A key that the type reads but never writes (`#[serde(skip_serializing)]`) is not offered. Example: the legacy wire `start`, which the load migrates into `picks`.
- A kind that the trace cannot read gets `"fields_incomplete": true`. The pinning test fails on it.
- The note of the tool tells what the new keys mean.
- `job.rs` gets 5 more lines (it was already over 400). The new logic is in the new module.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3449-list-op-type-fields.md`.

## Readings

- Each kind is traced. Only the height fields (`retract_z`, `bottom_z`, face `top_z`) have the type `"any"`, because `HeightDto` reads itself (untagged).
- The reply for one kind stays below the 4000-character budget. Measured replies: pocket 3604, sinker_side_burn 2123, wire_contour 2009, thread 1924, drill 1834, plasma_profile 1681, face 1563.

## Pinning tests

- `op_type_fields::list_operation_types_reads_every_kind_completely` (binary `mcp`, new file `crates/app/tests/mcp/op_type_fields.rs` in the `tests/mcp/` directory suite). This is the Done clause: every kind is traced, no kind is incomplete, and no field is listed twice.
- `op_type_fields::list_operation_types_names_the_optional_fields_and_enum_words`: pocket `tilt`/`rest`/`entry`, the Wire Contour extras and `tabs` shape, the plasma `feed`/`kerf`/`pierce_*`/`cut_height`, the drill `cycle` words, and the thread pass keys.
- The existing pins also pass: `mcp_wire_contour::list_operation_types_and_skill_match_wire_contour_dto_and_tool_law` (the wire fields are the same as the DTO keys), `mcp_wire_contour::list_operation_types_says_the_wire_kind_mounts_a_wire_tool`, `mcp_compact::list_operation_types_filters_by_kind_and_by_section` (4000-character budget), `break_through::issue_2441_mcp_list_operation_types_lists_break_through`.
- The pinning test also checks that the wire listing does not offer the legacy `start`.

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick` on the final head (Linux, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 1215 steps, 1212 pass, 3 fail, 0 stall. All app, motion, kernel, post, sim and gpu steps pass. The 3 failed steps are UI steps that need a wgpu adapter. This host has no display and no `xvfb-run`:
  - `ui suites: lib`: `egui_app::report_tests::*` and `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds` panic with `Failed to create render state: CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError("No adapter found")`.
  - `ui suites: egui_app` (3 headless start tests) and `ui suites: shell` (`headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`): the headless run returns 1 for the same reason.
  - This PR changes no UI file. A runner with a display must run these 3 steps again.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Serde cannot see a new optional key on the outer `thread` variant (a variant with a flatten), and the test does not find it. That one list of six names is written by hand.
- Wire `condition` is required by the add_operation check, not by serde. The listing shows it as an optional field with the default `""`, as before. It does not mark it as required.
- The issue asks for a unit for each field. Serde has no unit, so this PR does not add units.
- Light lane and heavy lanes: not run. No post or toolpath changed, and this is a P3 PR.
- PR #4007 touches other files (UI and `tests/mcp_rotary_flow.rs`). No overlap.

Changelog: MCP `list_operation_types` names every field that a kind accepts: optional fields are marked `optional`, enum fields list their `values`, and object fields show their `shape`.

Effort: medium

Fixes #3449

title: docs(decisions): path kernel K0 design record
body:
## What changed

This PR adds one design record: `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md`. It has no code. No kernel code starts before the maintainer approves this record.

Revision 2 takes in the maintainer's answers of 2026-11-25:
- "Replace the whole motion kernel in one go." Scope: 2D milling and 3D Pocket.
- A side branch and one switch. The program on `main` keeps the old behaviour until the new planner is proven.
- "The kernel should be its own crate."
- "At one point all 40+ motion types should move to the new kernel".

The record starts with a "Plain summary" that a machinist can read without the code.

## The six stages (plain words)

1. Area: the selection, the side that is material, and the stock and clamps.
2. Pass shape: rings, rows, a centre line, the line itself, or a helix.
3. Load control: none, trochoidal loops, or passes that hold the set load. It changes the pass shape only.
4. Order: the first pass (Inside or Outside) and the cut direction.
5. Links: the tool stays down. It lifts only with a reason on the status line.
6. Entry and exit: in air, in a pre-drilled hole, in a cut column, or a helix or ramp only into solid material. Else the operation is refused with a reason.

A strategy is a set of choices for these stages. The stages are a new crate (the crate `camcraft-pathkernel`). It depends only on `camcraft-geometry`, and `camcraft-motion` depends on it.

## The laws as checks

Each law of #4023 has a test shape and a measured value. The stage checks are in the new crate (K7, #4027). The checks of whole programs are in the old-against-new comparison in `camcraft-app`.

## The plan

- First replacement (phase 1): 16 kinds. These are the 2D milling kinds (Thread included), Bore and 3D Pocket.
- The work is on the side branch `side/path-kernel`. Each sub-PR targets that branch, with one issue each and the normal review rules.
- `main` is merged into the side branch after each related merge batch, and at least once a week.
- One switch (old or new) for all 16 kinds. It is old until the proof is complete.
- The proof: the law suite is green, and the test parts are measured old against new. Each catalog difference has a reason, and the verifier, light and heavy checks are clean. Then one switch-over PR goes to `main`, and the maintainer approves it. A second PR removes the old planners.
- Defects in the old planners are not patched there. An unsafe one goes to the maintainer as a question.
- #3750: its golden records of the old output are reused as the baseline. Its move of the old code on `main` is dropped.
- Roadmap: all 49 kinds in six phases (turning is phase 3). The record has a fit check of each later family and names what does not fit (tool tilt, a surface guide, the lathe plane, the two wire guides, cycles with no path, the sinker orbit). It also lists what phase 1 keeps open.

## Answered by the maintainer, 2026-11-25

The maintainer approved the design: "Yes, start". No question is open.
- The crate name is `camcraft-pathkernel`.
- Phase 1 has 16 kinds: Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Engrave, V-Carve, 2D Chamfer, Circular, Slot, Trochoidal slot, Trace, Slot Undercut, Thread, Bore and 3D Pocket.
- The phases: 1 is the first replacement; 2 is sheet cutting, Drill and Probe; 3 is turning ("Lathe earlier", then "Third"); 4 is 3D Finish and Deburr; 5 is wire and sinker; 6 is multi-axis and rotary.
- A "Side branch" rule goes into AGENTS.md first, and `side/path-kernel` is protected.
- The heavy `motion` and `app` steps run one time on the side branch before the switch-over.
- The maintainer reads the list of changed programs and approves the switch-over PR.
- One issue each for the five kinds with no issue: #4034 V-Carve, #4035 Slot, #4036 Trochoidal slot, #4037 Slot Undercut, #4038 Thread.

The work plane and the tool shape stay open from the start, because turning is phase 3.

## Tests

None. This is a docs-only PR. No build ran, and no gate is necessary.

Changelog: none
Effort: max

Fixes #4024

title: fix(adaptive): a 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point
body:
## What changed

The 2D Adaptive (`Adaptive2D`) takes a start point and an exit point (slice of #1448). The picks are the shared operation-level `picks` field of #3339. The command, the project file, the stamp and MCP `edit_operation` need no change.

- `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`: `Adaptive2D` is now `PickCapability::Region`. Only the Adaptive2D arm changes. The door refusal of the settings that cannot hold a pick is added to `pick_refusal`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_picks.rs` (new): the door (`adaptive_pick_refusal`), the picked entry, the piece order, the refusals, and the exit run back on the posted path (`exit_on_path`).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_hsm.rs`: `choose_entry` uses the start point as the seed. The pieces are ordered by `order_pieces`. A picked plan that falls back to the rings, or that keeps an overload, is refused by name. The budget unit test moves to `pocket_hsm_ring.rs` (the same test, so that the file stays under 400 lines).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs`: one hook after `emit_pocket_passes` for the exit.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_avoid.rs`: a pick in a "Do not touch" keep-out is refused with the item names.
- `crates/motion/src/approach.rs`: two runtime fields, `start_point` and `exit_point`. They are not saved. `crates/app/src/operation/adaptive_pick_op.rs` (new) lays the op's picks over the generation copy, or refuses them.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wcs_yaw.rs`: under a Z-rotated work offset the Adaptive picks turn into the generation frame, as the Slot picks do.
- UI: the Lead in / Lead out tab of the 2D Adaptive draws the Start point and Exit point groups (`start_exit_rows::region_groups`, drawn from `op_page.rs` because `mill2d_page.rs` is already over 400 lines). The viewport pick and the marks take the 2D Adaptive.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3327-adaptive-start-exit.md`.

## The law

- Start: the start point is the seed of the HSM plan. The helix (or the plunge) goes down there on each level, through the same entry law and the same triangle room as the automatic seed. The planner then grows the cleared area from that bore and measures each cut on its stock.
- Exit: the last pass of each level ends where the plan ends, on its closing ride along the walls. Then the tool runs back along the same posted moves in reverse (one round of the outer wall at most) to the point nearest the exit point, and climbs out there. A reversed line is the same line and a reversed arc is the same arc, so the run back cuts no new material and makes no feed-feed crossing. The piece nearest the exit point is cut last.
- The cut geometry does not change otherwise. Without a pick no new code runs.

## Refusals (by name, the pick is never moved, nothing is cut)

- `the start point (x, y) is outside the area the tool centre can reach ...`
- `the helix of radius r has no room at the start point (x, y) - the tool centre has c mm of room there and the helix needs n ...` (the plan's own 0.6 helix share)
- `the start|exit point (x, y) is inside the 'Do not touch' keep-out of <names> ...`
- `the exit point (x, y) is d mm from the closing ride of the last pass along the walls - the most is L ...` (L = 1.5 tool diameters + stock to leave, the contour's reach law)
- `the exit point ... is at the piece of the area where the cut starts, and n other piece(s) are cut after it ...`
- `an exit point needs the tool to climb out after the last pass of each level ...` (a level link that stays down)
- `the plan from the start point does not hold the optimal load (<planner note>) ...`
- `the HSM plan <reason> - the Offset rings or the trochoid that would cut the area instead do not take a start or exit point ...`
- At the door and at generation: a tilted (3+2) op, the Trochoidal method, Pass starts at Inside or Outside, a rest pass, and a start point with a Ramp or Arc entry.

## Readings

On a rectangle 60 x 40, tool D10, helix R2 (motion fixture):

- Automatic seed (30, 20): widest cut on the shape-mask meter 1.62 mm. Start point (15, 12): 1.79 mm. The limit in the test is 2.03 mm (the optimal load step with the plan's margin and the grid's).
- Start points (20, 15), (25, 20), (15, 12) are taken. A start point at (40, 25) makes the spiral keep "the least overload": it is refused. A start point at (12, 12) makes the plan cross itself: it is refused with that reason.
- Exit point (58, 20): each level ends at (55, 20). `crossed_pairs` is empty. The first try (a run back on the planner's walk, before the arc fit) read two crossings between the two arc fits, so the run back is made on the posted moves.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_levels` (`adaptive_picks` module):
  - `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` (two levels, no overload note, no crossing, widest cut under the limit)
  - `the_exit_point_is_where_the_last_pass_ends_on_each_level` (two levels, no crossing)
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
- `camcraft-app` `start_exit_shared` (`adaptive` module):
  - `the_entry_is_at_the_start_point_and_the_last_pass_ends_at_the_exit_point` (golden CL `adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`)
  - `the_picks_hold_under_a_90_degree_wcs_yaw`
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name_and_nothing_is_cut` (also the door: tilt, Trochoidal, Pass starts at Inside, Ramp entry)
  - `the_picks_ride_the_command_undo_the_file_and_the_stamp` (undo restores the previous path to the move; no pick plans the earlier path to the move)
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_adaptive_picks` (`edit_operation`, `get_job` reads them back, `undo` clears them, `list_operation_types` says `start: true, exit: true`)
  - `the_2d_adaptive_takes_a_start_and_an_exit_point`, and `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated)
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `the_2d_adaptive_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_and_takes_an_exit`, `a_2d_adaptive_takes_the_viewport_pick_and_shows_its_marks`

New test files join existing suites (`pass_start_levels/`, `start_exit_shared/`). No new top-level test binary.

## Goldens moved

None. One golden is new: `crates/app/tests/golden/adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`. A path without a pick runs no new code (see the gate: `golden_cl`, the example catalog suites).

## Not exercised

- The keep-out refusal has no pinning fixture. The code is one `contains` test on the keep-out region that `adaptive_spiral_avoid_on` already builds.
- The "climb out" refusal (a level link that stays down) and the "exit at the start's piece" refusal have no fixture.
- A plunge entry at a start point is taken by the door. Its first turn out of a tool-size bore is the planner's existing note, not an overload refusal; no fixture.
- The Trochoidal method stays refused (its seed is on the medial line). #3932 (the trochoidal entry slots to a wall) is a separate path; this PR does not change it.
- No machine run.

## Why `fix`

The issue is labelled `bug` (the 2D Adaptive refused a start and an exit point that #1448 says it takes), and the earlier slice of the same family (#3325, the Slot) shipped as `fix(slot)`. So this PR is a `fix` too, and it merges when it is reviewed.

## Gate

All on the final head `3764e7ed9` (the branch with `origin/main` merged in; one conflict in `start_exit_shared.rs`, where #3981 and this PR each added lines to the gate map and to one assertion; both kept), local Mac, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 875 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (83.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: pass_start_levels`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `golden_cl`, `ui suites: lib`, and the example catalog suites by name: `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (all ok).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the code head before the merge of main (the merge changed only test lines in `start_exit_shared.rs`).

Note: under load, the quick gate marked `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` slow (>60 s with 8 test threads) in the first run, not in the final run. The test plans one 60 x 40 area on two levels.

Heavy step: none. This is a P2 issue, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a targeted heavy step only to a P1 PR under the safety floor.

Changelog: The 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point: the entry goes down at the start point and the cleared area grows from there, and the last pass of each level runs back along its closing ride to the point nearest the exit point; a point that the plan cannot hold is refused by name.

Fixes #3327

title: fix(post): name the Agie post "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)"
body:
This PR builds on #4003 (issue #3996), which is merged. The branch started on the #4003 branch and then took `git merge origin/main`. The own commit is f6f40a28a; 028530986 is the merge of `main`.

## Decision

The contributor and the maintainer agreed the name on Discord on 25 Nov 2026. The post that writes AgieVision ISO, SBR and SBL job files for the AGIECUT Classic 2S is now "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)". Its refusals say "The Agie Wire EDM job requires ...". The record is `docs/decisions/4000-agie-wire-edm-name.md`.

## What changed, by class (issue #4000)

**B. Agie-specific texts with a generic name: renamed.**
- The post name `posting::agie::POST`: "Native wire EDM job files" -> "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)".
- `assets/posts/agie-native.cps`: the description, the `onOpen` refusal and the option group "Wire EDM technology" -> "AgieVision technology". The line count and the `throw` column do not change.
- 45 refusal and UI texts in 11 source files (and three module comments):
  - `crates/app/src`: `operation/agie_profile.rs` (21), `posting_agie.rs` (12), `posting.rs`, `posting_mounts.rs`, `posting_per_op.rs`, `posting_agie_group.rs` (1 each);
  - `crates/geometry/src/die_opening.rs` (1);
  - `crates/ui/src`: `post_dialog.rs` (2), `post_dialog_tabs.rs` (3: "AgieVision job files (ISO, SBR, SBL)", "the AgieVision control" two times), `state.rs` (1), `wire_page.rs` (the open-cut hint: "The Agie Wire EDM job requires both clamps ...").
- The `.mch` description of `agiecut-classic-2s.mch`.
- The 17 scripts in `examples/agie/` (`cps: "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)"`).
- `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`, `site/content/guide/check-and-post/posting.md`, `site/content/guide/operations/operations-edm.md`.
- `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` (a process file).

**C. Generic items with an Agie name.**
- The Wire page open-cut rows and the inspection controls: #4003 shows them only for Agie jobs. This PR renames only the hint text.
- `CommandKind::ImportAgieDrawing` -> `ImportInspectionDrawing` (an internal UI enum; it runs a plain DXF import). No MCP tool, CLI command or script verb changes.
- The old-name alias logic (`LEGACY_POST`, `current_name`, `current_ref`, `current_key`) moved out of `posting_agie.rs` into a new generic table `posting::aliases` (`crates/app/src/posting_aliases.rs`, `POST_ALIASES`). The project loader (`project/apply.rs`, `project/mount_dto.rs`), the option-key normalizer (`schema.rs`), `SelectPost`, `SetSetupPost`, `resolve_cps`, the post offer and the machine post check call it. No generic module calls `posting::agie` to resolve a post name.

**D. Stale documents.**
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: the wire section says that `WIRE_POSTS` has four entries, and has a new `agie-native.cps` paragraph.
- `site/content/guide/check-and-post/machines.md`: the wire row lists "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)" and the AGIECUT Classic 2S template.

## Compatibility

- Both old names stay hidden aliases: "Agie native wire EDM" (#3537) and "Native wire EDM job files". The table applies to the document post and the setup post in a project file, the option keys `builtin:<name>`, `SelectPost` and `SetSetupPost`, the script `cps:` value, the MCP post tools, the CLI and the machine `controller.post` value.
- A save writes the new name. The project file version does not change.
- Not changed: the condition ids, the MCP tool names, the CLI command, the module names, the golden folder names, and the script receipt value `"format": "Agie native wire EDM"`.
- The site anchor changes to `#agie-wire-edm-agievision`. The one link to the old anchor (`posting.md`) is updated.
- Old names still load, so this is not a breaking change.

## Goldens

- The posted job goldens do not change.
- Only line 2 of the 11 `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/agie-native/*.refusal` files changes (the `.cps` refusal text). The `(user.cps:16:9)` location does not change.

## Pinning tests

All in existing suites. `crates/app/tests/wire_post_alias.rs`:
- `the_new_name_is_listed_and_the_old_names_are_not` (pins the post list name);
- `the_alias_table_resolves_both_old_names`;
- `each_old_name_selects_the_new_post_by_command_script_and_lookup`;
- `a_project_saved_with_each_old_name_opens_posts_and_saves_the_new_name`;
- `an_option_map_under_each_old_key_normalizes_to_the_new_key`;
- `no_source_text_names_the_post_native_wire_edm` (the "Done means" text search of `crates/app/src`, `crates/ui/src`, `crates/geometry/src` and `agie-native.cps`; the alias table and the receipt value are the two kept lines).

Refusal texts pinned: `crates/app/tests/agie_native.rs` ("Agie Wire EDM jobs require default post options and One program output"), `plasma_post_refusals.rs` and `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` (the `.cps` refusal), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/agie_post.rs` (the dialog texts, plus the new pin of "A new job folder will contain the AgieVision job files (ISO, SBR, SBL).").
`mcp_wire_contour.rs` checks that SKILL.md lists no alias name from `POST_ALIASES`.

The ui `#[test]` count does not go down. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Gate (Windows, winbuild)

All on the final head `0285309868c5` (logs `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-4000-028530986*.log`, first line `HEAD 0285309868c56ac6ab6710cd750cba551f035ff0`), `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the geometry change makes quick fall back to batch. 1215 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 145.5 min. This includes `app suites: wire_post_alias`, `agie_native`, `conformance`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `plasma_post_refusals`, `post suites: comment_escape`, `script_agie_native`, `geometry suites: lib`, `ui suites: lib`, and `clippy -D warnings`.
- Example catalog suites by name (inside the same run): `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: ok.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Strict clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- P7, not under the safety floor: no heavy step.

## Not exercised

- No run on an AgieVision control: the job files do not change.
- The site build (Zola) did not run. The new anchor follows the default slug of the heading.

Changelog: The AgieVision post is now named "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)", and its refusals say "The Agie Wire EDM job requires ...". Projects, scripts and MCP calls with the old names "Agie native wire EDM" and "Native wire EDM job files" still open and post; a save writes the new name.

Process change: yes

Effort: medium

title: fix(mcp): the cli dials a ui link file only while its window holds its lock
body:
## What changed

Issue #3995: a person who reads a stale discovery file knows the token and can compute every token proof. A false server on the freed port of a crashed window could then receive the tool calls of `camcraft-cli --ui`.

This PR adds one rule for the whole class: the CLI uses a link file only while its window is proved alive.

- **The window holds a lock.** Each window takes an exclusive OS file lock on `<pid>.lock` in the link folder before it writes its link file. It holds the lock for its whole life. The OS releases the lock when the process ends, a crash included. A reused pid cannot hold the lock of an ended process. The window removes the lock file with its link file when it closes.
- **The CLI tests the lock two times.** It tests the lock before it dials an entry, and again after the hello. The second test closes the gap where the window ends during the exchange.
  - The lock is held: the entry is used.
  - The lock is free: the entry is stale. The CLI removes `<pid>.json`, `<pid>.sock` and `<pid>.lock`, logs a warning and never dials the address. It removes only these fixed names in the link folder, never a path read from the file.
  - No lock can be tested (no lock file, an error): the entry is unproved. The CLI logs why, keeps the file and never dials it.
  - When no window is left, the CLI exits 3. The message names each skipped entry and its reason. There is no silent fall-back to an unproved window.
- **std only.** The lock is `std::fs::File::try_lock` (`flock` on Unix, `LockFileEx` on Windows; stable since Rust 1.89, MSRV 1.90). No new dependency, and the same source on Windows, Linux and macOS. This avoids the `libc` / `windows-sys` declarations that held PR #3971.
- New module `crates/app/src/mcp/link_owner.rs` (the lock and the test). `link.rs` takes the lock in `open`; `link_client.rs` tests it in `connect`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3995-ui-link-owner-lock.md`.

## What stays open (Refs, not Fixes)

The lock proves that the window runs. It does not prove which socket on a TCP port answers. On Windows, a local process can share the loopback port of a running window (`SO_REUSEADDR`). The fix for that is the named-pipe transport with a check of the server process id. It needs a direct `windows-sys` dependency and a transport decision by the maintainer. It is filed as #4016 (P3, effort:max). On Unix the socket is in a 0700 folder, so this case does not occur there.

Thus this PR uses `Refs #3995`. The maintainer can close #3995 when he accepts that #4016 holds the rest.

## Compatibility

A window of an older build writes no lock file. A CLI of this build does not dial it: it exits 3 and says that nothing proves that the window runs. This is on purpose (see the decision record).

## Tests (final head)

Pinning tests (new submodule `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link_owner.rs`, in the existing `mcp_live` suite):

- `ui_link_owner::a_crashed_windows_file_is_removed_and_its_port_is_never_dialed`: a false server holds the port of a crashed window. It gets no connection. The link file and the lock file are removed. Exit 3 with "is stale".
- `ui_link_owner::a_false_server_that_proves_the_token_gets_no_tool_call_when_the_window_has_ended`: the false server reads the token and sends the correct server proof. The window ends during the hello. No tool call reaches the false server.
- `ui_link_owner::a_link_file_with_no_owner_proof_is_never_dialed`: a file with no lock file is never dialed and is kept. The CLI exits 3 and says why.

Changed tests in `ui_link.rs`: the forged-token test and the proofless false-server test now hold the lock, so that they still reach the token check. The wrong-token test also asserts that the window holds its lock and that the lock file goes when the window closes.

Results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 167 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 29.0 min. The plan is wide because the new `pub mod` line in `crates/app/src/mcp/mod.rs` maps to all 165 `app::mcp` suites. `mcp_live`: 25 passed. app lib: 311 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 19.6 min (the motion twins and `pocket_pass_start`; the diff does not touch them).
- Example catalog suites: not run apart from the quick plan (which includes `example_catalog`); no post or toolpath changed.
- No heavy step: this is a P3 PR.

## Not exercised

- Windows and macOS were not built or run. The lock is std code with no `cfg`, but `LockFileEx` behaviour was not observed on a host here.
- A second local user was not emulated.
- A file system where std file locks are not supported (`Unsupported`) was not tested. There the entry is unproved and skipped, by the code path of the no-lock-file test.

Changelog: `camcraft-cli --ui` uses a window's link file only while that window holds its lock. A stale file of a crashed window is removed and never dialed, and a link file without that proof is skipped with the reason.

Effort: high (not escalated).

Fixes #3995

title: feat(wire): arcs on model-based wire paths
body:
## What changed

A Wire Contour of a meshed model now posts its circles and fillets as G2 / G3 arcs. Before, they were G01 chords.

- New module `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/model_arcs.rs`. It reads the one closed model profile back as lines and arcs:
  - An arc stands on at least 3 facet chords. Each vertex is within 1 um of the circle. Each chord is at least 5 um long.
  - Each chord bows off its arc by no more than the model chord tolerance (`CHORD_CAP` 0.005 mm plus the model excess). A true polygon (an octagon) stays a polygon.
  - A run within 1 um of its end chord is a line. A radius over 1000 mm or under 0.01 mm is a line.
  - Split points on a chord (from the section or silhouette) are dropped first, the nearest one first.
- New module `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/model_tangent.rs`. A fillet end that meets a straight side within 1e-4 rad is made tangent to it. This prevents pivot arcs of no length (G1 blocks of no length).
- The chain goes to the analytic wire contour of #3937 (`wire_contour_arcs`): concentric kerf arcs, the same kerf and cover laws, the same refusals by name.
- `wire_op::generate_wire` takes the model chord (`None` for a selected DXF chain). Only the vertical, untabbed, one-profile cut reads arcs. Skims, tabs, burnout, exit pick, taper and 4-axis keep the polygon path (#3216, #3941).
- A profile with no fitted arc keeps the polygon cut byte for byte.
- `wire_verify`: a vertical model cut with arc moves is judged under the model chord plus the 1 um fit (0.006 mm). The verdict line says "kerf judged under the model's chord tolerance". The arcs pass between the facet chords and the true circle.
- `sim::verify::wire`: the undercut law of #3210 now runs only when the cut states a taper (`taper_chord && taper`).
- There is no B-rep path: the STEP and SolidCraft imports mesh each body, and the document keeps no analytic edge. The decision file has the reason.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3215-wire-model-arcs.md`.

## Readings

- A dia-8 hole meshed at 63 chords (die, start at the centre), generic ISO post:
  - two half arcs `G3 ... I-3.835 J0.` about (0, 0), radius 3.835 (4 - 0.165 kerf);
  - 2 straight blocks (lead in and lead out).
- The 40 x 20 die opening with 2 mm corners at 3-degree facets (`opening()` fixture of `wire_post`):
  - before: about 120 G1 chords;
  - after: 4 arcs about (+-18, +-8), radius 1.835, and 7 straight blocks (4 sides, one side split by the seam, lead in and out).
- The same posted program for the Sodick post (`G02` / `G03`).
- Verdict line of the `wire_verify` die: "kerf judged under the model's chord tolerance 0.0060 mm: the kerf enters the model's facets by at most 0.0007 mm" (the 3-degree chord sagitta is 0.68 um).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::model_arcs_tests` (11):
  - `a_meshed_hole_is_read_back_as_one_circle_and_cut_as_true_arcs`
  - `meshed_fillets_are_read_as_arcs_between_the_straight_sides`
  - `collinear_vertices_on_a_side_do_not_break_the_read`
  - `a_profile_with_no_arcs_is_not_read` (rectangle, octagon, no chord)
  - `degenerate_runs_stay_lines` (2-chord fillet, radius 5000 mm, 0.5 um wobble)
  - `a_vertex_off_the_circle_is_never_read_into_an_arc`
  - `the_laws_judge_the_read_arcs_and_catch_a_2_um_mutation` (kerf law refuses a 2 um shift; cover law refuses the arcs as chords)
  - `a_meshed_inside_fillet_tighter_than_the_offset_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_cluster_of_noise_vertices_is_never_read_as_a_tiny_circle`
  - `split_points_beside_polygon_corners_are_never_read_as_tiny_arcs`
  - `fillets_on_a_nanometre_lattice_meet_their_sides_tangent_with_no_pivot`
- `camcraft-sim` lib: `verify::wire::arc_tests::arcs_read_from_facets_pass_under_the_model_chord_on_a_vertical_cut`
- `camcraft-app` `wire_post` (new submodule `wire_post/model_arcs.rs`):
  - `a_meshed_hole_posts_as_two_half_arcs_not_chords` (ISO and Sodick, I/J checked)
  - `meshed_fillets_post_as_arcs_between_the_straight_sides` (ISO and Sodick)
  - `the_wire_laws_judge_the_read_arcs_under_the_model_chord`
  - `a_profile_with_no_arcs_keeps_its_polygon_cut`
- `camcraft-app` `wire_verify`: `a_correct_die_and_a_correct_punch_pass_and_name_the_piece_they_free` now also asserts the chord line.

## Goldens moved

None. No shipped wire golden uses a model with circles or fillets. The wire goldens (`wire_slug_punch.nc` for wire-iso and Sodick, `wire_contour_punch_skims.nc`, `wire_contour_open_cutoff.nc`, the `.cl` goldens `wire_contour_die`, `wire_contour_punch`, `wire_taper_punch`, `wire_4axis_punch`, `wire_open_cutoff`) are sharp polygons, skims, open runs, tapers or 4-axis cuts. They stay byte for byte, and this pins "a profile with no arcs does not change". The example catalog has no wire case.

## Not exercised

- No physical wire EDM machine or control ran the output.
- The EDM-T1/T2/T3 STEP files (MIT licence) are not used as fixtures. A third-party file needs its notice in the tree, and a STEP import makes a slow test. The tests build the meshed hole and fillets in code, at the importer's chord. A run of the EDM-T2 block through the app is not done here.
- The G-EDM post is not pinned by a new test here (it already writes G2 / G3 for the DXF arcs of #3937).

## Gate

All on the final head `a7a32e421c4eca96459da0015e720d71efc370a3` (each log starts with that SHA):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 184 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 31.5 min (log `gates/3215-a7a32e421.log`). The plan includes the pinning suites, every wire and Sodick / G-EDM / Agie suite of the gate maps, and `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (all ok).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed (log `gates/3215-a7a32e421-light.log`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Before the commit, the wire suites ran one by one (`wire_post`, `sodick_wire_post`, `g_edm_post`, `wire_contour`, `wire_verify`, `wire_verify_tol`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_taper*`, `wire_sharp_corners`, `wire_readers`, `wire_stamp`, `feature_pick_wire`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_fans`, `sodick_wire_passes`, `sodick_alc400g`, `sodick_wire_dielectric`, `wire_iso_decimal`, `agie_native`, `wire_post_alias`, `wire_tool`, `edm_machine`, `solid_law_goldens`): all ok.

P6: no targeted heavy step (only a P1 PR under the safety floor runs one).

Note on file length: `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs` was 506 lines on main and is 508 now (one parameter, one `allow`). The new logic is in its own motion modules.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a Wire Contour of a meshed model posts its circles and fillets as true G2 / G3 arcs (read back from the facets within the model chord tolerance), not as G01 chords.

title: feat(multiaxis): the Rotary Flow multi-band and single-helix kernel
body:
﻿## What changed

The picked Rotary Flow guide chains now read as ONE ordered set. The
chain-set law lives in a new `rotary_flow_set` module of the motion
crate; the band loop of `rotary_flow` gains the shared-boundary dedup,
the single-chain lap, the sense normalization, and the set refusals.

- **Multi-band.** Three or more ordered chains machine one band per
  adjacent pair, and the SHARED boundary chain is cut once: band k > 0
  starts at its first interior pass. Band k - 1's last pass already
  walked the shared chain at the same stations, the same push-out and
  the same climb setting, so nothing is lost.
- **Single helical chain.** A lone chain machines the full revolution:
  the kernel synthesizes the second boundary as the chain's own next
  lap, one whole turn on in the unwrap's own theta (`th + TAU`), every
  other coordinate held. The lap takes no whole-turn alignment (it is
  exact by construction). The lap's two edges are the SAME world curve,
  so the closing pass is dropped - the picked chain emits once.
- **Sense normalization.** A chain wound against its pair is walked
  backwards, said in the notes. This supersedes #2824's opposite-sense
  refusal: the feature layer reads a chain's direction from the mesh,
  never from the pick, so the refusal fired on legal picks the user
  could not reverse (the probe on the bar showed the end-face rings
  extracting wound -TAU while the profile rings extract +TAU). The raw
  pairing of two oppositely wound chains twists the band a whole turn;
  the reversal untwists it. Review rework (PR #4018 review, item 1):
  the normalization now runs ONCE over the complete ordered set
  before any band is cut (`normalize_set`), and the SAME normalized
  guide bounds both adjacent bands - never a per-band copy, which
  left the next band's lower boundary at the raw winding and flipped
  the second band's cutting direction without a change to climb.
- **Ring lap guard.** Review rework (item 2): a single guide that
  turns about the axis at one axial station and one radius - a closed
  ring or an open arc of one - is refused by name before a pass is
  generated (`refuse_ring_lap`): its lap reads a positive angular
  width but sweeps no band area, and the pass family would repeat one
  closed cut. A guide that advances in station or in radius sweeps a
  real band and passes.
- **Refusals, all by name.** Chains that meet or cross are refused at
  the shared spot (the exact segment-pair law, Ericson 5.1, at the
  corner-lattice dust). Consecutive bands whose mean developed offsets
  oppose (dot < 0) are refused as a set out of band order. A
  perpendicular turn is not a doubling back: bands may tile around a
  corner. Zero-length, non-finite and duplicate chains keep the #2824
  refusals.

## Geometry readings

- The lap's developed width is exactly `R_ref * TAU` at the chain's own
  outermost radius: `dth = TAU` and `dv = 0` at every matched place, so
  `cross_width` reads one full revolution. The pass count divides it at
  the stepover, and the emitted count is `ceil(width / step)` - the
  closing pass is the picked chain itself.
- The multi-band dedup emits `count_0 + count_k - (k)` passes over k
  bands: band k > 0 takes `count - 1`, and the first interior pass sits
  one stepover or less from the shared boundary, so the coverage never
  opens a gap.
- Refusal readings: the meet test is the exact segment-pair closest
  distance (four endpoint candidates plus the clamped interior solve,
  Ericson 5.1 as the guard cites it); the backtrack test compares the
  mean developed offsets of consecutive pairs and refuses only a
  strictly negative dot.

## Pins

- Motion, `tests/rotary_flow/bands.rs`: three ordered root helices cut
  two bands in 7 passes (4 + 4 - 1) with pairwise-distinct landings;
  one root helix covers the full revolution in 26 passes, the first
  pass winding exactly `TAU`, gouge-free per the station pin; a ring
  that crosses a corner chain refuses at the crossing's own spot.
  Review rework pins: the middle pick reversed holds the direction
  of every pass of every band for BOTH climb settings (aligned
  control and mixed winding, pass by pass); a single closed ring
  refuses the zero-area lap family by name; a single open ring arc
  refuses the same.
- Motion, unit: the lap morph, the meet law with its witness, the
  backtrack law, the pass-count law, the backward walk (twice is the
  identity, the knots stay ascending), the set normalization (mixed
  winding resolved once, the cascade judged against the normalized
  neighbour), the ring lap guard (a ring refuses, a helix and a
  radial arc pass).
- App, `tests/rotary_flow_band.rs`: three ring chains cut two bands,
  the plunge count agrees with the bands' own stated counts, no two
  passes land on one station, the notes state the shared boundary and
  the sense walk.
- App, `tests/rotary_flow_lap.rs` (new file; reason below): one
  meridian chain machines the full revolution in 19 passes, one
  landing per azimuth, lap note stated; the meridian-plus-ring set
  refuses at the shared corner, with no path cached.

## What was not exercised

- The app-level pins run on the turned bar, not a helical screw: the
  app's slicing refuses open meshes, and a closed screw fixture with
  sharp helical edges is its own fixture work. The helical single-chain
  and multi-band coverage is pinned at the motion level on the groove
  fixture (one-turn and three-turn rotors, station and swept-ball
  proofs).
- The heavy lanes are not run (#3556: no PR gets the full heavy lanes;
  this is a P7 under the safety floor, so no targeted heavy step is
  owed). The light lane ran partially green (motion light: lib, the
  adaptive troch twins, app light: pocket_pass_start); its
  all-binaries release build step failed on machine disk during the
  run, not on code - the same build passed clean after a full rebuild
  of the touched crates.
- No example catalog case exercises Rotary Flow, so their outputs
  cannot change; the quick plan still ran all three catalog suites,
  green.
- The quick gate's app prebuild wedged once (#3675) and the app suites
  were run one by one instead: all 20 planned suites green, clippy
  `-D warnings` clean on both touched crates.
- Review rework head (99283bc76, after the merge of main 49bfcaea8):
  the rework gate ran `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` (683
  passed, 0 failed, 22 ignored), `cargo test -p camcraft-motion
  --test rotary_flow` (14 passed, 1 heavy-ignored), `cargo test -p
  camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_band` (7 passed), `cargo test -p
  camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_lap` (2 passed), the three new
  tests by name, and clippy `-D warnings` clean on
  `camcraft-motion --all-targets` and on the touched
  `camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_band` binary. The light lane of
  the first head stands; the rework diff touches only the flow
  kernel and its own pins, and the review re-runs what it needs.
- The crossing between NON-adjacent guides that the review named
  non-blocking (pre-existing on main) is filed as #4032 and stays
  out of this branch.

## File note (#3187)

`crates/app/tests/rotary_flow_lap.rs` is a new top-level test file: the
rotary domain keeps one top-level file per topic, and a second file
holds these laws so `rotary_flow_band.rs` stays under the 400-line
ceiling.

## Changelog

Rotary Flow: three or more ordered guide chains machine one band per
adjacent pair with the shared boundary cut once; a single guide chain
machines the full revolution as its own next lap; the complete set is
wound one way before the bands are cut, so a reversed pick never flips
a band's cutting direction; a single ring guide - closed or an open
arc - is refused by name, its lap sweeps no band area; chains that
meet or cross, and sets out of band order, are refused by name.

Fixes #2829

title: test(3d): re-pin the pocket3d_hsm bore after the solidcore bump
body:
## What changed

The heavy step `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm` was red on `main`. This PR finds the commit and updates the pins with proof. It changes no product code.

- `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`:
  - The Linux mesh pin changes from 6228 to 5232 facets.
  - The count pin changes from (3158, 3130, 1141) to `BORE_PIN` = (4688, 4660, 1980) on Windows x86_64, Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64.
  - The exactness tests also reject the reading from before the bump.
- `docs/decisions/3886-pocket3d-hsm-pin.md`: the decision record.

## The first bad commit

The first bad commit is the merge of PR #3802 (df899f029, the solidcore bump). I did not need a full bisect. Linux x86_64, release, with a print-only probe in the test (not committed):

| Commit | Facets | (moves, planar, arcs) | Warnings | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 940cc5d0e (parent of df899f029) | 6228 | (3158, 3130, 1141) | 0 | pass |
| df899f029 (#3802 merge) | 5232 | (4688, 4660, 1980) | 0 | fail |
| baad348f1 (`main`) | 5232 | (4688, 4660, 1980) | 0 | fail |

On `main` the Linux run fails first at the mesh pin (line 80, 5232 against 6228), as sn3ro reported. All other asserts before the count pin pass.

## Why the new counts are correct

PR #3802 changes no planner code. It changes `Cargo.lock`, `crates/kernel/Cargo.toml` and `geometry/src/step_diag.rs`. Only the mesh changes. Measured per level (planar feeds, arcs, planar feed length):

| Level | Before (6228 facets) | After (5232 facets) |
|---|---|---|
| Z 15 | 397, 72, 334.31 mm | 1933, 918, 999.92 mm |
| Z 10 | 1933, 918, 999.92 mm | 397, 72, 334.31 mm |
| Z 5 | 403, 79, 327.81 mm | 1933, 918, 999.92 mm |
| Z 0 | 397, 72, 334.31 mm | 397, 72, 334.31 mm |

Each level after the bump takes one of the two plans that the planner already made before the bump. The new mesh changes which levels take the long plan. It does not make a new plan. After the bump:

- every level verifies clean against the part solid (no warnings);
- no level falls back to rings;
- no planning budget note shows;
- the levels are Z 15, 10, 5 and 0.

There is no gouge.

The long plan cuts about 3 times the feed of the short plan for the same disc. Its feeds also stop 0.153 mm short of the wall in -Y. This defect is older than the bump: the old pin already held it at Z 10. It is a planner algorithm defect (`effort:max`), so this PR does not fix it. It is filed as #4010 (P3).

## Platforms

- Linux x86_64: measured in this work (table above).
- Windows x86_64: the issue comment of 2026-11-24 measured (4688, 4660, 1980) at 6d0381f19 and 2e2d40cb3, which are after the bump. The test does not assert the facet count on Windows.
- macOS arm64: NOT measured after the bump. Its pin follows Windows and Linux, because macOS had the same triple before. A macOS run must confirm it.

## Tests

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`): `app suites: pocket3d_hsm` ok. This includes `the_linux_x86_64_bore_count_pin_is_exact` and `the_stamp_tells_the_hsm_plan_from_the_rings`.
- Heavy step (`cargo xtask gate release --only "app heavy: pocket3d_hsm"`): ok on Linux x86_64. `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` passes. The known-fail #1950 test is skipped by the gate, as before.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): 6 of 6 steps ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test pocket3d_hsm -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The Windows and macOS runs of the updated test. `the_windows_x86_64_bore_count_pin_is_exact` and `the_macos_arm64_bore_count_pin_is_exact` were not compiled on this host.
- The example catalog suites: no post or toolpath code changed.

Changelog: none

Effort: medium (no escalation)

Fixes #3886

title: fix(motion): eliminate full-width cuts at ring merges
body:
## Summary

- Collapse interior Clipper lattice micro-steps (`< 5e-5` mm) in `ring_fill::clean_walk` before `share_ends` so segment tangents stay stable on rings and `WALL` loops.
- Extend `ring_fill` with recursive binary sub-levels up to `RING = 16` (`split_band`), `merge_flank_hits` checks in both Inside and Outside order (`level_flanks::full_width_flanks`), dual reach (`tool_r` for ring gaps, `2.0 * tool_r` where flanks fire), and `tail_extension` (`<= 3.5 * tool_r`) to `c`'s boundary.
- Reject boundary `edge_route` chords in `level_order` and `ring_links` (`chord_full_width`) when both `0.9 * r` flanks cut unmachined stock, and walk the full multi-vertex `via` path in `level_order::join`.
- Record design choices in `docs/decisions/3788-ring-merge-waist.md` (clean-room implementation from Held 1991 and existing flanks and keep-down laws).

title: fix(sim): a box side a few ulps longer than whole cells gets no extra column
body:
## What changed

One rule for every stock or verdict lattice sized from a length: a side within a relative 1e-9 of a whole number of cells gets that whole number of cells; a real part of a cell still gets its cell.

- `stock_sim::kernel::cells_across(extent, cell)` counts cells across a length.
- `stock_sim::kernel::edge_cells(v, cell, upper)` (new) is the same law for an edge locked to the origin.

Sites on the rule:
- `Dexel::block` (column stock).
- The field box gate and the field cylinder gate (`backend_build.rs`). The cylinder gate counts the circumscribed square the column arm builds.
- The exact carry read `History::read` (`carry_exact.rs`), with `.max(1)`, so a thin box keeps one column.
- The field arm's verdict lattice `lattice_of` (`march.rs`), by `edge_cells`.
- The side-on slabs of a cut body (`carry_side.rs`), with `.max(1)`.
- The mesh stock gate on both arms, `from_facets` (`cut.rs`, `backend_build.rs`), plus the one cell of margin each side.

Left as they are, because they hold no stock and the case cannot arise there: the edge-break window in `wall_anchor.rs` divides by 256 (exact), and the `scan.rs` envelope grid has a full margin of air beyond the part.

## Readings

A 12.7 mm side two ulps long over a 0.254 mm cell:
- Block and exact carry: 50 columns (was 51). No material past the box edge (was up to one cell).
- Field verdict lattice: 50 columns (was 51, against the column arm's 50).
- Side-on carry of a cut body: 50 slabs (was 51).
- Mesh stock on either arm: 52 columns with the margin (was 53). A strip 4094 cells a few ulps long now builds on both arms (was refused as 4097).

## Pinning tests

`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cell_count_tests.rs`, synthetic shapes only, 9 tests:
- `a_whole_number_of_cells_up_to_rounding_is_that_number`
- `no_material_stands_past_a_box_edge_read_a_few_ulps_long`
- `the_cell_ceiling_gate_counts_the_same_columns`
- `the_exact_carry_read_counts_the_blocks_columns`
- `the_field_box_gate_counts_the_same_columns`
- `both_cylinder_gates_count_the_same_columns`
- `the_field_verdict_lattice_over_a_box_has_the_column_arms_columns`
- `the_side_on_carry_slices_a_height_a_few_ulps_over_whole_cells_into_whole_slabs`
- `both_mesh_stock_gates_count_the_same_columns`

Each site set back to its old count turns its test red; with the rule, all 9 pass.

## Gates

On the final head c2dcb516c (upstream/main merged in):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 83 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.6 min).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cell_count_tests`: 9 passed, 0 failed.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes and the light gate (release build of the app).
- The GUI.

## Related

- #4047: a cylinder stock over about 1000 cells across builds on the column arm and is refused on the field arm by the per-facet cell budget in `field_gen.rs`. Measured on main; not changed here.

Effort: high (stock simulation is under the safety floor).
Changelog: Stock: a side a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells no longer gets an extra column, slab or verdict cell, on either backend.

Branch: upstream/main merged in (plain merge); the diff is 9 files: the 7 source files above, the test file, and the one `mod.rs` line that registers it.

title: feat(cli): --skill <folder|claude|copilot> install writes an AI agent skill
body:
## What changed

Part 2 of #3751: `camcraft-cli --skill <folder|claude|copilot> install [--dir <path>] [--user] [--force]`. The command writes an AI agent skill that teaches the CLI. Part 1 (`--ui`, PR #3861) does not change.

- New lane `crates/app/src/cli_skill.rs`. It is a `HELP_LANES` entry, so the help tests check it. `cli.rs` gets the usage lines and one dispatch line, and stays under 400 lines (393).
- One source for the skill text: the hand-written body `crates/app/src/cli_skill.md` (our own text), then a generated "Command reference". The reference is `TOP_USAGE` and each `HELP_LANES` usage text, exactly as the binary prints them. Thus a new lane or flag shows in the skill with no edit.
- Targets:
  - `folder`: `<dir>/SKILL.md` with the Agent Skills header (`name`, `description`). `--dir` is necessary.
  - `claude`: `.claude/skills/camcraft-cli/SKILL.md` in the current folder (or `--dir`). With `--user`: `~/.claude/skills/camcraft-cli/SKILL.md` (`HOME`, else `USERPROFILE`).
  - `copilot`: `.github/instructions/camcraft-cli.instructions.md` with `applyTo: "**"`, from the GitHub Copilot repository custom instructions documentation. The user's own `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is not touched.
- The command never replaces a file silently. When the target file is there, it exits 1, names the path, writes nothing and names `--force`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3751-cli-skill-install.md` (target paths and their sources, the default scope, the overwrite rule, no MCP tool).

## Pinning tests (`camcraft-app`, suite `cli`)

- `skill_folder_target_writes_skill_md_into_the_given_folder`
- `skill_claude_target_writes_the_project_skill_or_with_user_the_home_skill`
- `skill_copilot_target_writes_an_instructions_file_for_all_paths`
- `skill_install_never_replaces_a_file_without_force`
- `skill_text_names_every_cli_lane_and_no_other` (the drift test: the skill names each lane in `HELP_LANES`, and each `camcraft-cli <word>` in the skill is a lane that exists)
- The existing `every_subcommand_answers_help_and_names_its_flags` and `every_listed_command_is_a_help_lane` now walk the `--skill` lane too.

Each target test runs the real binary in a temporary folder, with `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` set to a temporary folder.

## Gate

Quick gate on head `5f4316003`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`, `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`): 10 steps, 0 failed.
- `app build`, `app suites: lib`, `ai_guide`, `cli` (18 passed), `default_machine_missing`, `example_catalog`, `first_part_programs`, `mcp`, `mcp_verify`, `regression_models`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The light lane did not run: no light twin covers this change (no toolpath, post or geometry code).
- Note: two earlier gate runs with sccache failed at the build step with `error[E0463]: can't find crate for camcraft_cl` (a bad cached rlib, not this diff). A `cargo clean -p` of our crates and a run without sccache fixed it.

## Not exercised

- No Claude Code or Copilot session read the installed files. The tests check the paths and the headers only.
- Windows and macOS: not built. The code uses only `std::fs` and `std::env`.
- No heavy lane and no light lane step: the change touches no toolpath, post or geometry code.

## MCP

No MCP tool and no follow-up issue. The lane writes a text file for an agent. It changes no document state and has no undo, so it is not a command in the sense of "Everything Is a Command". An MCP agent already reads the tool table with `camcraft-cli mcp reference`.

## Notes

- New tests join the existing top-level `cli` suite (`crates/app/tests/cli.rs`, 386 lines). No new test binary.
- No process file changes: the repository's own `.claude/skills/` is not touched.

Changelog: `camcraft-cli --skill <folder|claude|copilot> install` writes an AI agent skill for the CLI (lanes, exit codes, examples and the full help text). It refuses to replace an existing file without `--force`.
