title: fix(tools,sim,ui): read corner_r for dovetail cutters
body:
## What changed

Dovetail cutters (`ToolKind::Dovetail`) now read `corner_r` across geometry, verification, stock simulation, and the UI:

- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `Head::Dove` stores `{ cot, corner_r }`. `Undercut::rho` evaluates the corner arc up to `s_tan = c * (1 + sin t)` and the tangent flank above `s_tan`. `Undercut::contact()` returns `(r, corner_r)`.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `undercut::refusal` checks `corner_r` in `[0, diameter / 2]`, checks `s_tan <= flute_len + NECK_MEETS`, and checks neck clearance against the rounded flank.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs` and `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`: `head_outline` and `Tool::meridian` emit the rounded corner arc and straight flank.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/`: `Cutter::atoms` emits `Prof::Zone` (`[0, s_tan]`) and `Prof::Dove` (`[s_tan, flute_len]`), or a single `Prof::Zone` when the flank top meets `s_tan`. `swept::rho_expanded` and `rotary_geom::shapes` handle `Prof::Zone`. `Frame` moves to `probe_frame.rs` under the 400-line rule.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/`: `SdfTool::Dovetail` and `RevKind::Dove` add `corner: f64`. `field_dove::dove_dist` computes the exact Euclidean SDF of the rounded dovetail head.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`: `tool_settings_grid`, `tool_summary`, `tool_cutter_params`, and `tool_undercut_row::seed` show and preserve `Corner radius` for `ToolKind::Dovetail`, while keeping it hidden and zeroed for `TSlot`, `Keyseat`, and `Lollipop`.
- `docs/decisions/4004-dovetail-corner-radius.md`: records the unattended design decisions.

## Readings

For the `#4004` dovetail cutter (`diameter = 19.05 mm`, `tip_angle = 60 deg`, `flute_len = 9.525 mm`, `shank_d = 8.0 mm`):

- `corner_r = 0.0 mm`: top radius is `4.026 mm` (`contact = (9.525, 0.0)`). The 24 mm wide, 30 deg slot verifies clean and posts.
- `corner_r = 0.254 mm`: top radius is `4.212 mm` (`+0.186 mm` wider; `contact = (9.525, 0.254)`). The 24 mm slot catches `Warning::Gouge` and holds the post.
- `corner_r = 3.0 mm`: top radius is `6.222 mm` (`+2.196 mm` wider; `contact = (9.525, 3.0)`). The 24 mm slot catches `Warning::Gouge` and holds the post, and field stock removes the wider flank and rounded bottom corner.

## Verification

- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass (0 warnings).
- `camcraft-tools` lib tests (`undercut` 15, `meridian` 13, `tool_sanity` 7, `cutter_profile` 4): pass, including `a_rounded_dovetail_reads_its_corner_radius_and_widened_flank` and `a_dovetail_corner_radius_refusals_name_the_rule`.
- `camcraft-sim` lib tests (`verify::probe_meridian_tests` 1, `verify::swept::tests` 2, `stock_sim::field_dove::tests` 2, `stock_sim::field_solid::tests` 3): pass, including `a_lifted_dovetail_corner_zone_is_never_grown_smaller_than_its_solid` and 19,980-sample `the_dovetail_distance_matches_a_dense_boundary_reference`.
- `camcraft-sim` integration tests (`undercut_laws` 16, `verify_avoid_undercut` 4, `undercut_fixture_envelope` 3): pass, including `a_rounded_dovetail_flank_gouges_the_24mm_slot_and_cuts_wider_in_field_stock` and `a_rounded_dovetail_keeps_clearance_on_its_corner_and_flank`.
- `camcraft-motion` tests (`machining2d::undercut` 9, `golden_undercut` 4): pass, including `a_rounded_dovetail_shifts_by_its_widest_corner_and_keeps_z_at_station`.
- `camcraft-app` integration tests (`mcp_slot_undercut` 8, `mcp_undercut_fixture` 3, `stock_play` 8, `stock_play_partial` 4, `tool_gate` 10, `tool_law` 7): pass, including `a_dovetail_corner_radius_catches_the_24mm_slot_gouge_and_holds_the_post`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib tests (`tool_undercut` 6, `tool_cutter_params` 6, `ball_corner_tests` 4, `tool_properties` 9): pass, including `dovetail_properties_and_editor_edit_flank_angle_and_corner_radius` and `switching_from_bull_nose_to_dovetail_keeps_valid_corner_r_and_clears_oversized_one`.

## What changed

First slice of #3330: the 5-Axis Contour (`Contour5D`) takes a start point and an exit point. MultiAxisContour is not in this PR. It uses a different planner (the drive-curve `contour_curve`), and the issue asks for one kind for each PR.

- `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`: `Contour5D` is now `PickCapability::Ring`. The UI rows, the MCP `edit_operation` schema and `list_operation_types` read this capability, so they take the picks with no other change.
- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/ring_seam.rs` (new): `RingSeam`, `waterline_seamed`, and the law. `waterline` moves into this file with the same body.
- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/rings.rs`: one hook for the start and one hook for the exit in the ring loop (`emit_rings_seamed`). `None` walks every ring as before.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/contour5d.rs`: `contour5d_seamed`. The same stamp poses the seated ladder.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the Contour5D arm reads `RingSeam::of(&params.path_picks())`. The arm is shared with Parallel5D, and Parallel5D does not read the seam.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3330-contour5d-picks.md`.

## The law (Contour5D)

- Start: each closed ring of the waterline ladder starts at its point nearest the pick (XY). The seams of all levels align toward the pick. The ladder does not read the pick Z.
- Exit: each closed ring cuts its full lap. Then it continues along its own vertices to its point nearest the exit pick, and the tool retracts there.
- An open run (a ring that the overhang column law cut into pieces) keeps its ends.
- The cut order and the cut geometry do not change. Only the seam moves, and the exit adds a re-trace over cut material.
- The tilt limit, the shank dodge and the centre-cutting guard run on the seated path. Thus they are judged at the pick too.

## Refusals (by name, the pick is never moved)

- `start point (x, y) is d mm from the nearest ring of the ladder, farther than the L mm a start point may sit from it` (L = 1.5 tool diameters). The same text applies for the exit.
- `start point (x, y): the ladder has no closed ring to start on`. The same text applies for the exit.
- `start point (x, y): the plunge column to the ring at z Z crosses the part there`. Without a pick, the loop rotates the entry to a clear vertex. With a pick, it refuses.
- `exit point (x, y): the retract column from the ring at z Z crosses the part there`. The column is judged up to the clearance plane.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `multiaxis` (module `multiaxis/seam.rs`):
  - `contour5d_start_point_seats_every_ring_at_the_pick`
  - `contour5d_exit_point_ends_every_ring_at_the_pick`
  - `contour5d_exit_point_under_a_canopy_is_refused_by_name` (new)
  - `contour5d_pick_far_from_every_ring_is_refused_by_name`
  - `contour5d_without_a_pick_is_the_automatic_ladder_byte_for_byte`
  - `cuts_ride_the_ladder` samples each level cut every 0.25 mm and requires each sample on the automatic ladder within `TOL`. Before, it read only the end point of each move.
- `camcraft-motion` lib (`finishing3d::ring_seam_tests`, new):
  - `exit_retract_column_through_a_canopy_is_refused_by_name`: the exit retract column law on the untrimmed ladder, with a canopy above the exit point.
  - `nearest_states_a_segment_end_as_the_next_segment`: a foot at a segment end is the start of the next segment, so the run-on adds no lap at the seam.
- `camcraft-app` `start_exit_shared` (module `start_exit_shared/contour5d.rs`):
  - `contour5d_starts_at_the_picked_start_and_leaves_at_the_picked_exit`: now also samples each level cut of the started and the picked ladder every 0.25 mm against the automatic ladder (within the 0.1 mm operation tolerance).
  - `contour5d_refuses_a_pick_far_from_every_ring_by_name`
  - `contour5d_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `undo`, `redo`)
  - `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated: Contour5D is Ring)

## Mutations (review of `9d11b0ae5`)

Each mutation was applied locally, run, and reverted. None is committed.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `ring_seam.rs` `run_on`: `poly.extend(lap)` removed | RED: motion `contour5d_exit_point_ends_every_ring_at_the_pick` ("a cut stands 0.165 mm off the automatic ladder"), app `contour5d_starts_at_the_picked_start_and_leaves_at_the_picked_exit` ("a cut stands 0.160 mm off the automatic ladder") |
| 3 | `rings.rs`: the exit retract column check removed | RED: motion lib `exit_retract_column_through_a_canopy_is_refused_by_name` |
| 4 | `ring_seam.rs` `nearest`: the snap at `t = 1` removed | RED: motion lib `nearest_states_a_segment_end_as_the_next_segment` |

## Goldens moved

None. A path without a pick passes `None` to the ring loop. This is pinned byte for byte at motion scale, and the example catalog suites are green (see the gate).

## Not exercised

- The blocked plunge column refusal at a picked start has no pinning fixture. Without it, the loop falls back to the old rotation to a clear vertex, which is safe.
- Through `waterline_seamed`, the exit retract column refusal cannot be reached: the column trim checks the same column every 0.25 mm at an equal or larger radius, so a canopy opens the ring first and the exit pick has no closed ring (pinned by `contour5d_exit_point_under_a_canopy_is_refused_by_name`). The exit law is pinned on the untrimmed ladder.
- The other multi-axis kinds stay `PICK_OWED`: MultiAxisContour, Parallel5D, Swarf, AdvancedSwarf, RotaryContour, RotaryParallel, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Flow5D.
- No machine run.

## Gate

All on the final head `fdce232c8`, local Mac. The branch has `origin/main` merged in: one conflict in `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared.rs` (the Gate map header and one panic text of the capability test). Both sides kept; the panic text is main's.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 215 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.1 min). The plan includes `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: multiaxis`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, and the example catalog suites by name: `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (6.1 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (on `e344b7aba`; the last commit changes only the decision file).

Heavy step: none. This is a P2 issue, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a targeted heavy step only to a P1 PR under the safety floor.

title: feat(multiaxis): Rotary Flow stock simulation parity and radial C unwind
body:
﻿#3999 has merged; this branch refreshes against `main` and is retargeted. The editor work for the multiaxis page rides the stacked PR for #2827.

## What changed

- **The parity proof.** `rotary_field_parity.rs` proves `Stock::simulate_rotary` against the independently written swept-ball/flute law for `OpParams::RotaryFlow`, at the verdict class, beside the Parallel/Contour/Offset lanes. A `Kind::Flow` fixture joins `common/rotary_bar.rs`: the laid bar, 72 facets (the density the band suite proves on - a 16-gon ring's 22.5 deg knots swing the pose past the kernel guard's drift margin), the band picked between the neck ring at x 2 and the top cap rim at x 16 - the pair whose feature chains advance about the axis in the same sense.
- **The lift.** `stock_sim_rotary::rotary_kind_lift` answers `Ok(())` for `RotaryFlow` on the measured parity. The eye (`stock_view`, `stock_play`) cuts the kind; the column verdict still refuses it by name, as it refuses every rotary kind. `ROTARY_KIND_UNMEASURED` stays for the next kind; no kind carries it today.
- **The radial C unwind.** `stamp_spindle_c`'s boolean became the enum `Unwind { NoProof, Axial, Radial }`: Rotary Contour unwinds over the axial plane, Rotary Flow on the retract cylinder, Parallel and Offset are refused where they would rewind - by name, the words now naming both proven kinds. `cl::unwind_c`'s cut-reach reading gained the mirror of its own plunge-start rule: a feed a rapid follows ENDED at rest, not in a cut, so the flow kernel's cut-feed exit off a pass no longer poisons the rest cylinder. Every inserted orbit chord is still judged by the verifier, the solid bar and the post gate.

## The parity readings (release, the laid bar's neck band)

- `Stock::simulate_rotary`: 2,063 moves, 1,559 turning -> 35,491 sub-chords, half-angle 1.990e-3, centre sag 5.940e-6 (within the 1e-4 pose law), wall 46.6 s, 1.312 ms per sub-chord.
- Height parity: 168 sphere-cut tops within **1.269e-5** of the law, bound **2.011e-5** (centre sag 5.94e-6 + `FIELD_VERDICT_EPS` 1e-5 + the law's sampling sag 4.2e-6); 1,015 standing tops exact; 0 flute-cut, 0 grazing, 0 sliver columns.
- Sign parity: 7,053 probed cell centres, **0 misses**, worst 0.000e0, band 1.832e-2.
- The eye's own class: 2,131 sub-chords in 3.0 s (1.414 ms each).

No epsilon was widened; `FIELD_VERDICT_EPS` and the sag bounds stand as the other kinds left them. The readings and the fixture's band choice are recorded in `docs/decisions/2828-rotaryflow-parity.md`.

## The pins

- `cl::rotary_unwind`: a feed-retract link shape (the flow kernel's own) unwinds at its cylinder with `radial = true`, is refused by name without it; the at-or-inside-the-cut-radius refusals still refuse.
- `rotary_gate` unit pins: the gate unwinds the radial path for Rotary Flow (a stated C rate given, #906), refuses it for Rotary Contour, refuses Parallel/Offset by name.
- `rotary_flow_band`: the full-ring band on the shipped millturn (C -360..360, stated rates) generates, unwinds at its radial retract links, every C inside the travel, the chain held, C continuous, a rewind orbit spanning a whole turn on the retract cylinder; a stated travel with no C rate refuses the rewind by name (#906); a pass wider than a narrow travel refuses with no clear link inside it.
- `rotary_field_parity` quick tests: the column verdict refuses Flow by name; the eye draws the lifted kind.

## What was not exercised

- The two new heavy lanes (`the_flow_kind_reads_the_radial_law`, `the_flow_kinds_eye_cost_is_measured`) are `#[ignore]`d and run at the cut; both were run locally in release to take the readings above.
- Posting the unwound flow band through the lathe post is held out: the radial field law reads the ball on the band's convex crease ring as a gouge past its allowance - the finding #2826 already reports, and that warning blocks the post of a clean unwind.
- The flow unwind tests joined `rotary_flow_band.rs`, not `c_axis_unwind.rs`: `c_axis_unwind.rs` sits at 356 lines and the flow fixtures (band picks, bench C) already live in the flow suite. Both gate modules' unit tests moved to sibling files (`rotary_gate_tests.rs`, `rotary_unwind_tests.rs`) to hold the 400-line law. A top-level test binary was added: `rotary_flow_band.rs`. Reason: the band fixtures and grammar pins span the motion kernel, the app project grammar and posting; their natural siblings in the flow suite are already top-level.
- The editor findings (items 1-4 of the review: screenshots, the stated-axis arm, the retract-radius control, the tilt wording) land via the stacked PR for #2827, whose branch owns `crates/ui/src/egui_app/multiaxis_page.rs`; its screenshots cover the before/after views. This PR's breaking-change commit is `0085ba36e` (`BREAKING CHANGE:` footer: the project file moves from v81 to v82; a v81 reader refuses the new files).
- The `graphify update` step did not run: the graphify binary is not installed in this environment; `graphify-out/` is generated output and nothing committed reads it.

Changelog: Rotary Flow: the field eye now cuts the kind (parity proved against the radial law), and on a spindle C with stated travel the band unwinds by whole turns at its radial retract links instead of refusing.

Fixes #2828

title: fix(ui): show Agie-only controls only for an Agie job
body:
## Report from the maintainer

The maintainer said that the "Export Agie inspection setup" text and button "appear everywhere". Agie-only controls must show only for a job for the Agie control (AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S, the native Agie post).

## What showed where, and why

| Place | Before | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Post page of a setup, section "Agie nominal inspection" (`agie_inspection.rs`) | Shown for each setup. On another machine it said "Mount the AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S machine on this setup ...". | The section returned early only when there was no setup AND no Agie machine. |
| Operation page, action "Export Agie inspection setup" and the hint "Nominal inspection only ..." (`op_page.rs`) | Shown on each normal DXF die cut, on each machine. | `has_agie_inspection_source` is true for each active die-side Wire Contour on one DXF sketch chain. It does not read the machine. |
| Wire page, open cut (Left/Right), rows "Both pieces clamped through all passes", "Stock centered in installed XY travel" and the hint "Agie open cuts require ..." (`wire_page.rs`) | Shown for each post. | Only the native Agie post reads the two flags (`agie_profile.rs`). |

Other places were checked. The post dialog already shows its Agie rows only for the native Agie post (`posting::agie::is_native`). `browser_files.rs` only maps `ImportAgieDrawing` and `ExportAgieInspection` to browser refusals; the only UI that starts them is the Post page section and the operation action. The File and Import menus have no Agie item. MCP is not changed.

## The rule and the change

- `agie_mounted(world, ctx)`: the setup context mounts the AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S machine of the wire EDM kind. This is the same test that `prepare_inspection` uses for the export.
- `agie_job(world, ctx)`: `agie_mounted`, or the setup context posts with the native Agie post.
- The Post page section (and its "Import DXF drawing" button) draws only when `agie_mounted`. The "Mount the AGIECUT ..." hint is removed.
- The export action and its "Nominal inspection only" hint show only when `has_agie_inspection_source` is true and the operation's own setup is `agie_mounted`.
- The Wire page open-cut rows and hint show only when `agie_job`.

For an Agie setup, nothing changes: the section, the import, the export and the rows show as before. No command, MCP tool, project field or name changes. Decision record: `docs/decisions/3996-agie-only-ui.md`.

The rename of the Agie post and its texts is tracked in #4000. This PR renames nothing and keeps the present wording of each Agie text.

- `saved_selected_opening_exports_zero_steps_through_the_desktop_action`, `setup_post_inspection_fields_and_submit_fit_the_visible_panel`, `unassigned_inspection_opening_survives_undo_redo_and_project_reopen` (unchanged)

The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by 5. No snapshot PNG changes.

title: feat(wire): a tangent arc lead-in and lead-out
body:
## What changed

Wire Contour has an opt-in tangent arc lead-in and lead-out. The straight lead stays the default.

- **Parameter.** `WireContourOp.lead_arc_radius: Option<f64>` (mm). `None` is the straight lead. The project file writes `lead_arc_radius` only when it is set (serde default), so old files read the straight lead and do not change.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` takes `lead_arc_radius` (a number, or `null` for the straight lead). `list_operation_types { "kind": "wire_contour" }` lists it. The `camcraft-mcp` skill row names the field and its refusals.
- **UI.** The Geometry tab has a "Tangent arc lead-in and lead-out" check and a "Lead arc radius" row. The check seeds 0.5 mm. Apply uses the existing undoable `EditOperationParams`.
- **Motion.** A new module `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_lead.rs` builds the leads. `wire_contour_arcs_led(chain, p, lead)` takes the lead. `wire_contour_arcs` keeps its signature and the straight lead. `arc_cut.rs` changes only in the lead code of `wire_contour_arcs`; `stitch` does not change. The branch merges `origin/main` with PR #3988; the one conflict was in the test helpers of `wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs`, and both sides are kept.

## The lead geometry

- The seam stays the path's nearest point to the start hole (the #3937 rule, with the +X rule for a hole at the centre of a circle).
- The lead circle has the stated radius. It touches the path at the seam, with its centre on the waste side: left of the walk for a die, right for a punch.
- Lead-in: a straight from the hole to the point where the tangent from the hole touches the lead circle, then an arc on the circle to the seam. The wire meets the path in the path's own direction.
- Lead-out: the mirror. The wire continues on the lead circle at the end of the lap, then goes back to the hole on a tangent straight.
- The two leads close a small waste piece between them. The path note says so. The wire verdict counts it as a second freed piece, and the capture statement covers it (a selected DXF cut needs that statement).
- The author confirmed this lead-out design: a tangent lead-in and a tangent lead-out, the small extra waste piece stated in a path note, and two freed pieces under the capture statement. A lead-out back along the lead-in arc was not chosen, because the wire would turn 180 degrees at the entry point.

## The radius rule and the refusals

The stated radius is never changed, and the cut never falls back to the straight lead silently. Each refusal is by name:

- A radius that is not larger than the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap). The command door refuses it when the operation is made, edited or given a new tool, after the condition resolves: `wire_sketch_arcs::lead_arc_radius_refusal`, called from `wire_gate`. The create, edit, retool and MCP paths all go through that gate. The generator keeps its own check for a loaded file or a machine whose condition changed later.
- A start hole that is not outside the lead circle. On the normal through the seam, the hole must be more than twice the radius from the path.
- A lead span nearer the profile than the kerf offset (an arc that crosses the profile or the waste-side clearance). With the nearest-point seam, a generated lead stays in the disc about the hole that the path only touches. Thus this check is a guard. Its unit test reads it on a seam that is not the nearest point.
- At the command door and at generation: the arc lead with an open run, a 4-axis cut, a no-core burnout, tabs, skims, a taper, or an exit pick.
- At generation: the arc lead on a profile that is not a selected DXF chain (a model's section).

The lead circle's centre is written on the CL lattice (1e-6 mm). The arc radius is then the distance from that centre to the seam. Thus the arc ends on the seam exactly and is tangent there within the lattice.

## Alignment with the start and exit points (#3332, #1448)

The lead uses the start pick in `picks` as its hole. It adds no second notion of where the wire enters or leaves. The lead shape is an operation parameter beside the picks, as #1448 describes ("leads in at that point"). The exit pick of #3332 keeps its straight lead-out. The analytic route already refuses an exit pick, so the arc lead with an exit pick is refused by name. A later change can give the exit's lead-out the same arc.

## Posts

No post changes. The leads are line and arc moves, so the generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM posts write the lead arcs as G2/G3 (G03 on Sodick) with I/J. The first cut move is the tangent straight from the hole, so the Sodick rule (no arc as the first cut move) holds.

## Readings

Die circle, radius 5, hole at its centre, radius 1 lead (`wire-iso/wire_dxf_die_circle_arc_lead.nc`):

```
G0 X6. Y5.
G1 X9.574 Y4.035
G3 X10.835 Y5. I0.261 J0.965
G3 X1.165 Y5. I-4.835 J0.
G3 X10.835 Y5. I4.835 J0.
G3 X9.574 Y5.965 I-1. J0.
G1 X6. Y5.
```

The lead arc centre is X9.835 Y5. (radius 1, on the waste side of the entry X10.835 Y5.). The entry point is the same as with the straight lead.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_lead_tests.rs` (motion lib):
  - `a_die_circle_is_entered_and_left_on_tangent_arcs`
  - `a_line_and_arc_punch_is_entered_and_left_on_tangent_arcs`
  - `a_hole_too_near_for_the_lead_circle_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_radius_not_over_the_kerf_offset_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_lead_that_would_cross_the_profile_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_lead_arc_moved_two_microns_into_the_product_is_caught_by_the_kerf_law` (the mutation)
  - `the_straight_lead_is_the_default_and_unchanged`
- `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arc_lead.rs` (in the existing `wire_dxf_selection` suite):
  - `die_circle_with_an_arc_lead_is_tangent_verified_and_posts_its_goldens` (ISO, Sodick, G-EDM)
  - `line_and_arc_punch_and_a_polygon_take_the_arc_lead_and_pass_the_verdict`
  - `a_hole_too_near_and_a_pair_the_arc_lead_is_not_cut_with_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_radius_at_or_under_the_kerf_offset_is_refused_at_the_command_door` (review finding 1: a radius equal to the C110 offset of 0.165 mm and a radius of 0.1 mm; the edit and the create are refused; the operation and the undo history do not change; a radius 0.001 mm over the offset passes)
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_wire_contour/arc_lead.rs` (in the existing `mcp_wire_contour` suite): `edit_operation_sets_the_arc_lead_radius_and_refuses_what_it_is_not_cut_with` (MCP round trip, door refusal, a radius of 0.1 mm refused at the door with the operation unchanged and no undo step, model refusal, undo).

title: fix(ui): start the GPU layer playback from the Simulate view (S3c)
body:
This PR is slice S3c of the GPU stock sim (#2629), for #3336. It does not close #3336. Read "Not exercised" first: no hardware adapter was available.

## What changed

- The Simulate view starts the playback worker in the layer mode of PR #3882 when two things are true. The window shell made a cutter on the render device. The stock eye has a GPU trace pass.
- In each other case the CPU playback of before starts. Nothing changes for these users.
- New module `crates/ui/src/play_layer.rs`:
  - `render_cutter` makes the cutter. It runs `cut_onto_or_cpu_on` (the S2 and S3a kernel) on the render device of the window. It makes no second device (#3589).
  - A software adapter (`DeviceType::Cpu`) gets no cutter. `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` gives no cutter. A device without compute gives no cutter. One log line names the reason.
  - The kernel is compiled on the playback worker at the first batch, not on the UI thread.
  - `cut_input` maps `TwinItem` to `CutItem` field by field.
- The view pass (`view_pass.rs`) tells the state if the eye traces on the GPU. If the eye holds a layer frame but marches it on the CPU, the layer playback ends and the CPU playback starts. The status line says this one time.
- `PlayWorker::spawn_layered_precalc` (app): the layer mode with the calculation before playback (#2181).
- `FieldPlay::set_layer` (app) keeps the layer mode off when no operation has an f32 twin.
- The bench `stock_play_cost_bench.rs` gets a layer-mode walk (`playback_cost_in_the_layer_mode`, ignored, release).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3336-gpu-layer-playback.md`.

## Cause

- PR #3878 and PR #3882 added the kernel and the layer mode. No caller turned the mode on. `crates/ui/src/actions.rs` called `PlayWorker::spawn_precalc` only.
- `set_layer` left the layer mode on with zero layer operations. Each frame was then a whole-layer pack (11.2 ms on fig8) in place of a patch (0.13 ms).

## Finding: the reference programs of #3336 do not reach the GPU

- The fig8 2D Offset and the 3D Pocket each have arc moves. The f32 twin refuses an operation with an arc (`an arc move has no twin; only linear moves cut here`). The operation stays on the f64 field.
- Reading (release, this branch, Linux, one run): fig8 15.6 ms for each move, Pocket 5.3 ms for each move. These are the values of the reading of 2026-11-22.
- Arcs on the kernel are slice S4 (#2628). This PR gives a gain only for a program whose operations have linear moves only, with a ball or flat end mill, on a hardware adapter.

## Tests

Pins (each failed before the fix):

- `play_layer_tests::the_transport_starts_the_layer_playback_when_the_eye_traces_on_the_gpu`
- `play_layer_tests::a_still_frame_of_the_layer_playback_cuts_nothing_again` (the counter test of #3336 on the layer path)
- `play_layer_tests::an_eye_that_cannot_hold_the_layer_frame_ends_the_layer_playback`
- `play_layer_tests::an_eye_that_does_not_trace_on_the_gpu_keeps_the_cpu_playback` (the CPU fallback test of #3336)
- `play_layer_tests::the_layer_playback_ends_only_for_a_held_frame_off_the_gpu`
- `play_layer_tests::a_twin_item_maps_to_the_kernel_item_field_by_field`
- `play_layer_tests::a_software_adapter_gets_no_kernel_by_name`
- `stock_play_picture::the_layer_playback_with_the_calculation_before_playback_draws_the_field_picture`
- `stock_play_picture::a_program_with_no_twin_op_keeps_the_layer_mode_off`
- `play_layer_gpu::the_gpu_cutter_draws_the_cpu_twin_layer_and_a_device_without_compute_takes_the_cpu_law` (ran on llvmpipe; the kernel answered, `CutPath::Gpu`; 7 seek positions within the twin margin; a device without compute gave the CPU layer)

Red before the fix:

- Without the start in `follow_playhead`: the first three pins failed (`the worker runs in the layer mode`, `the layer playback cut up to the playhead`, `assertion failed: state.layer_play.on`).

Mutations:

- `start_cutter` without the `eye` and `refused` conditions: 3 pins red (`an_eye_that_does_not_trace_on_the_gpu_keeps_the_cpu_playback`, `an_eye_that_cannot_hold_the_layer_frame_ends_the_layer_playback`, `the_layer_playback_ends_only_for_a_held_frame_off_the_gpu`). Restored: green.
- `set_layer` without the no-twin condition: `a_program_with_no_twin_op_keeps_the_layer_mode_off` red. Restored: green.

Original gate results on the final head `3aebb3a38`, base `upstream/main` d80dc6944:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 30 steps, 0 failed; 2,154 passed, 15 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 69 steps, 1 failed. The failure is `pocket3d_hsm` `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`: `the mesh behind the Linux path pin`, 5232 against 6228 facets. It fails at the model import, before a toolpath or a playback. `pocket3d_hsm` is red on main (#3886). This PR changes no import and no toolpath code.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored.

## Goldens moved

None. `example_catalog` ran green and `git status` showed no changed file. The PR changes display playback only. It changes no toolpath, no post and no verdict code.

## Review evidence for PR #4001

`play_layer_gpu.rs` is the only new top-level test binary. It needs its own process to keep one test and one graphics device alive (#3589, #3605). This device isolation avoids two live devices in one process.

### Before and after screenshots

- Before: runtime source from `upstream/main` `d80dc6944f912171a06029f635e0450c505d44a9`. ![Simulate before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/359114e474e4d01f3e4c79a8dfe5feff19ef3690/pr-4001/simulate-before.png)
- After: PR head `3aebb3a38500aae1c2356c11e0fc21b13eb78b04`. ![Simulate after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/359114e474e4d01f3e4c79a8dfe5feff19ef3690/pr-4001/simulate-after.png)
- Scene: a 12 x 12 x 20 mm stock with a staged Face1 operation and a 4 mm flat end mill. The playhead is paused at 14.2815 of 23.8025 seconds (60%). The camera and layout are identical. Both captures produced the same pixels; the CPU fallback picture stays unchanged.
- Actual render adapter in both captures: `llvmpipe (LLVM 19.1.7, 256 bits)` via Vulkan, software. CPU playback cuts the stock in both captures. The stock composite is ready before each capture.

The screenshots use the same Simulate scene and seek position. They render the shipping shell layout and the shipping viewport pass with the stock composite. They use an offscreen capture harness. They do not show a native window or prove the hardware GPU layer path.

### Checks repeated on 2026-11-25

The code head is unchanged: `3aebb3a38500aae1c2356c11e0fc21b13eb78b04`. The base is current `upstream/main` `d80dc6944f912171a06029f635e0450c505d44a9`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 30 steps, 0 failed; 2,154 passed, 15 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 69 steps, 68 OK, 1 unexpected failure, 0 stalled (44.5 minutes). The failure is `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`: the import facet pin reads 5232 against 6228. This is the same failure reported in the original body (#3886).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored. No golden or catalog file changed.

### Evidence checks

These two review findings require PR text and screenshot evidence. They require no production code changes. A code pin and a code mutation do not apply. The PR text check fails when these sections are removed and passes when they are restored.

## Not exercised

- No hardware adapter. This machine has llvmpipe only. The kernel on the render device of a real window did not run. The frame rate with the GPU cutter is not measured. The parity on a hardware adapter (#2629, precondition 1) is not proven; the layer is display only.
- The window shell path (`shell_window.rs` to `shell_cutter`) and the view pass rule did not run in a window. The rule itself (`LayerPlayback::must_end`) and `play_layer::end` are pinned without a window.
- A second thread that polls the render device while the UI thread draws did not run.
- No path choice by batch size (#2629, precondition 3). Only the adapter type decides.
- The browser shell gets no cutter. The wasm build was not run.
- The screenshots above show the software adapter path. No hardware adapter was available to show the GPU layer playback.
- If a layer worker runs with zero layer operations and the eye falls to the CPU march, the playback restarts one time without need. The picture stays correct.

## Overlaps

- PR #3963 changes `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in a different function. This PR adds one field to `State`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Simulate: the stock playback cuts operations that have linear moves only (ball or flat end mill) with the GPU kernel on the window's graphics device, when it is a hardware adapter; the CPU playback runs in each other case.

title: fix(2d): the Face raster takes a start pick and an exit pick
body:
## What changed

The Face operation takes a start pick and an exit pick. It reads them from the operation-level `picks` of PR #3871.

- **Start.** The raster starts at the corner of the face region that is nearest the start pick. The edge row at that corner is cut first, away from the corner. The rows then step to the far edge.
- **Exit with a start.** The exit pick names the side where the last row ends. An even row count ends on the side of the start corner. An odd row count ends on the opposite side. A side that the row count cannot reach is refused by name.
- **Exit alone.** The planner chooses the start corner that ends the last row at the corner nearest the exit pick.
- **No pick.** The path is the automatic raster, byte for byte.
- **Rotated work offset (review round 1).** A work offset with a Z rotation carries the geometry into the generator frame. `wcs_yaw::rotate_params` now carries each start and exit pick with it. The rule reads `OpParams::path_picks_mut`, so it holds for each kind that stores picks.
- **2D Contour under a rotated work offset (review round 2).** The same rule changes one more kind. Before, a Contour start or exit pick did not turn into the generator frame, and the cut entered on the wrong wall. Now the cut enters and leaves at the picks. This changes the Contour toolpath and its posted G-code for a job that has a pick and a Z-rotated work offset.
- **Rows cut short (review round 1).** The picks are judged again on the rows that each level cuts, after the holes law and the "Do not touch" keep-out (`face_raster::Raster::held`). The first piece of the first row must start on the side of the start pick. The last piece of the last row must end on the side of the exit pick. If not, the cut is refused, and the text names the blocked pick. The protected area stays clear.
- **Tilted (3+2) Face.** A pick is refused by name, as on the tilted 2D Contour.
- **Page.** The Face Geometry tab shows typed Start point and Exit point groups.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` sets the picks. Its schema text names the Face rule. `list_operation_types` reports `start_exit` as taken for Face.

The refusal text for a blocked pick is: `Face: the exit point is blocked at Z -2.000 - a hole or a protected 'Do not touch' item takes the last row beside it, so the raster cannot exit at that corner; clear or move the exit point, or free the row`.

The refusal text for the row count is: `Face: the exit point is nearest the other side - a raster of 6 rows from the start corner ends at the start corner's own side; clear the exit point, start at the other corner of the first row, or change the stepover (the row count)`.

Files:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face_raster.rs` (new): the planning rule.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face.rs`: the new entry point `face_picked`. `face_over_kept` calls it with no pick. The file has 400 lines.
- `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`: Face answers `PickCapability::Raster`. A tilted Face refuses a pick.
- `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_turn.rs`, `generate.rs`: the Face arm passes the picks. The picks are turned into the laid frame of an open boundary.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wcs_yaw.rs`: the picks go into the generator frame with the geometry.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`: the schema text.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_rows.rs`, `mill2d_page.rs`: the typed groups.
- `docs/decisions/3326-face-start-exit.md`: the decisions.

## Cause

`face_over_kept` set the first row and its direction from the Climb switch only. `KindInfo::pick()` answered "not taken" for Face, so the command door refused each pick.

## Where the issue is silent

I chose the smallest rule in each case. The decision file gives the reasons.

- An exit pick without a start pick: the planner chooses the start corner that reaches the exit. The issue names the start corner as a cause of the refusal, and here the user stated no start corner.
- An exit pick with a start pick is judged by its side only (the words of the issue). When the exit pick is nearer the first row, the path has a note that says where the raster ends.
- A pick at equal distance from two sides takes the low side.
- From a high Y corner the rows are the same band in the opposite order. The band is not mirrored, so the rows never change.
- The pick is stated in the setup's frame. It is carried into the frame of the face region (an open boundary turn, a rotated work offset) before the corner is read.
- A row that a keep-out cuts short, but that still starts (or ends) on the picked side, is accepted. A row that is taken is refused. The planner does not move the entry or the exit to a different row.
- The Face page has typed rows only. A viewport Pick button is not in this change: `start_exit_pick` writes to the 2D Contour only, and PR #3978 changes that file.

## Tests

Pins (all new, all green on the final head):

- `crates/motion/tests/face_start_exit.rs` (14 tests):
  - `start_at_the_low_x_low_y_corner_matches_golden`, `start_at_the_high_x_low_y_corner_matches_golden`, `start_at_the_low_x_high_y_corner_matches_golden`, `start_at_the_high_x_high_y_corner_matches_golden` (one golden CL each)
  - `an_exit_on_the_side_the_last_row_reaches_is_taken`
  - `an_exit_the_row_count_cannot_reach_is_refused_by_name`
  - `an_exit_alone_ends_the_last_row_at_its_corner`
  - `an_exit_beside_the_first_row_says_where_the_raster_ends`
  - `no_pick_is_the_automatic_face_to_the_byte`
  - `blended_turns_stay_outside_the_footprint_from_every_corner`
  - `the_holes_bound_the_same_row_pieces_from_every_corner`
  - `the_lead_runs_on_along_the_picked_first_row`
  - `a_pick_no_planner_can_read_is_refused`
  - `a_keep_out_that_takes_a_terminal_row_refuses_the_blocked_pick_by_name` (review round 1)
- `crates/app/tests/face_start_exit.rs` (10 tests):
  - `the_raster_enters_at_each_picked_corner`
  - `the_picked_corner_over_the_stock_matches_golden`
  - `an_exit_the_rows_cannot_reach_is_refused_by_name_and_a_reachable_one_is_cut`
  - `undo_and_redo_restore_the_previous_path`
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_face_picks`
  - `a_tilted_face_refuses_a_pick_at_the_door`, `a_file_with_a_pick_on_a_tilted_face_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_air_entry_runs_on_along_the_picked_first_row`
  - `the_registry_says_the_face_takes_a_start_and_an_exit`
  - `a_rotated_work_offset_reads_the_picks_in_the_setup_frame` (review round 1)
- `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_turn.rs`: `a_start_pick_names_the_part_corner_under_every_turn`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_tests.rs`: `the_face_geometry_tab_states_and_clears_its_start_and_exit`

title: feat(ui): tool Properties summary, holder pick and Body section in the tool library window
body:
U4b of #3663. This PR finishes the U4 surface moves that #3931 held back.

## What moved where

- **Properties (saved tool):** the page is a read-only summary (`tool_summary.rs`): type, sizes, holder, spindle rpm, feed, material group, tool number, and the side preview. The button "Edit in tool library" opens the tool library window on the tool. The Properties subject does not change. The summary has no Apply.
- **Shape window:** the holder library picker is removed. The window keeps the Body and Profile tabs (drawn holder, cutter).
- **Tool library window, Tool tab:** a folded "Body" section under "Holder and stick-out". It has the stand-in `holder_d` / `holder_len` rows and the body section (Import body…, placement, Pick tip / Pick axis, Apply body, Convert to profile, pieces). It uses the window's own body draft (`ToolEditorView::body`), which `with_library_draft` swaps into `tool_body_ui`. A turning tool shows the Body section and no picker.
- **Tool library window, Recipes tab:** the rest of the old Cutting data group follows the table: the tool's own spindle rpm and feed, the lathe rows and centre cutting (`tool_settings_grid::cutting_base`).

## Why the three parts are in one PR

The three parts are one move of the same fields. If the Properties groups go first, the holder and body fields have no editor. If the window gets the Body section first, the same fields have two editors. One PR keeps each field in one editor at each commit (user decision: fewer PRs).

## Kept, and why

- **New-tool form:** Properties keeps the full grid and Add tool. The window has no editor for a tool that is not in the document.
- **"Edit tool shape" on the summary:** the shape window edits through Properties' draft (`tool_ui`), so its door stays beside that draft.
- **Body tab of the shape window:** it stays. It is the input of "Convert to profile" beside the Profile tab, and about 30 tests drive it. The two body drafts are separate, so the two places do not mix. A follow-up can remove it.

## Commands and MCP

No new command. Each change uses the command that it used before: `ChangeTool`, `ReshapeTool`, `SetToolNumber`, `SetToolBody`, `SetToolBody::library` and the piece commands. No MCP tool is owed. Decision: `docs/decisions/3930-tool-properties-summary.md`.

## Tests

New pinning tests:
- `tool_library_assembly::the_body_section_imports_into_the_window_draft_only`
- `tool_library_assembly::a_turning_tool_has_the_body_section_and_no_holder_pick`
- `tool_properties::edit_in_tool_library_opens_the_window_on_the_tool`

Moved tests (old → new; the intent is kept):
- `tool_holder::the_holder_library_is_the_first_thing_the_shape_editor_shows` → `tool_holder::the_holder_library_heads_the_assembly_group_not_the_shape_window`
- `tool_holder::{apply_holder_lands_the_bt30_er20_and_undo_restores, a_shank_the_holder_cannot_take_is_refused_by_name, the_projection_lands_through_apply_holder_and_undoes, the_picker_lists_the_tts_holders_and_names_the_collar, one_weldon_row_for_each_taper_takes_the_bore_of_the_shank}`: same names, now in the window's assembly group
- `tool_holder_reference::{a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited, the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it, holder_picker_uses_label_left_rows}`: same names, now in the window (Body section, assembly group)
- `tool_properties::properties_tool_apply_and_undo_use_the_command_history` → `edit_in_tool_library_apply_and_undo_use_the_command_history`
- `tool_properties::tool_settings_form_a_label_left_grid_in_collapsible_groups` → `tool_settings_form_a_label_left_grid_in_the_window_tabs`
- `tool_properties::properties_shows_the_settings_and_the_shape_window_holds_the_shape` → `properties_shows_a_summary_and_the_shape_window_holds_the_shape`
- `tool_properties::tool_page_keeps_apply_and_add_tool_beside_close_without_scrolling` → `tool_page_keeps_its_buttons_and_add_tool_beside_close_without_scrolling`
- `waterjet_recipe::waterjet_properties_apply_preserves_recipe_refusal` → `waterjet_window_apply_preserves_recipe_refusal_across_a_browser_pick`; the other three waterjet tests keep their names and use the Recipes tab
- Same names, now drive the window: `tests::tool_settings_edit_live_and_the_shape_editor_follows_its_tool`, `tests::inch_mode_drag_keeps_px_parity_and_types_onto_the_lattice`, `ball_corner_tests::*`, `tap_hand_tests::tap_hand_checkbox_stages_until_apply_and_undo_restores_right`, `tool_cutter_params::the_editors_apply_carries_a_landed_cutter_onto_new_numbers`, `tool_undercut::dovetail_properties_and_editor_edit_flank_angle_without_corner_radius`
- Layout: `layout_page_tool` (summary anchors), `layout_window_tool_shape` (no picker), `layout_window_tool_editor` (Body section under the group), `structural::tool_editor_structure`

The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes from 1829 to 1832. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Readings

- Windows (winbuild). Branch head `94012ffed` is trial-merged with `origin/main` `d80dc6944` as `005aec1fe`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`): 18 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 6.4 min. The steps are the ui build, ui lib (123 s) and 16 ui integration suites. Log: `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-3930-94012ffed.log`.

- Heavy and light lanes: not run. This is a P4 UI PR, and no post or toolpath code changed.

## Screenshots

Seeded document, tool EM-0600-4FL, shell 1600 x 1000.

| Properties | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3930/before-properties.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3930/after-properties.png) |
| Shape window | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3930/before-shape-window.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3930/after-shape-window.png) |
| Tool library window, Tool tab (after: Body section open) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3930/before-library-tool-tab.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3930/after-library-tool-tab.png) |

## Not exercised

- A body import through the file dialog in the window. The test uses `import_tool_body_from` with a path.

Changelog: The tool Properties page is now a summary with an "Edit in tool library" button. The holder pick moved from the tool shape window to the tool library window, and the window's Tool tab has a folded Body section (holder cylinder, body import and placement, pieces).

title: refactor(ui): view cube, marker and axis inks are theme tokens
body:
Stacked on #3992 (which is stacked on #3990). This branch starts from `issue/1120-handle-inks`. Its own commit is the last one (114f7b171). Review that commit only. Merge #3990 and #3992 first.

## What changed

The second family of #1120: the view cube, marker and axis inks.

- Twelve colour tokens join `Tokens`. Each is also a theme-file key (`colors.<name>`):
  - the view cube and its nav buttons: `cube_edge`, `cube_label`, `cube_glyph_on`, `cube_glyph_off`;
  - the corner hint: `viewport_hint`;
  - the playback tool marker: `marker_stem`, `marker_ring`, `marker_dot`;
  - the axis triad of the Axes button and the handles: `axis_x`, `axis_y`, `axis_z`;
  - the hover gold of the view cube dot and of the machined facet: `viewport_hover`.
- The dark table holds the old dark-ground set of `ground_ink::cube_ink`. The light table holds the old light-ground set. No pixel changes.
- `ground_ink::cube_ink_on(&Tokens, light)` builds the `CubeInk` from a token table. `cube_ink(light)` keeps its signature and reads the built-in table of that ground. The face and button greys stay numbers chosen by the ground.
- `viewcube.rs` and `shell.rs` read `viewport_hover` for the gold. The facet veil keeps its alpha of 90 over the token's RGB.
- The ground rule in `theme_files/overlay.rs`: before this change the cube chose its set by the viewport ground, not by the base. When a theme file makes the ground light on the dark base (or dark on the light base), each of the twelve keys that the file omits takes the value of the built-in table of that ground. A key that the file sets always wins. `docs/user-guide/themes.md` says so.
- The built-in tables write `from_rgba_premultiplied(a, a, a, a)` for the old `from_white_alpha(a)`, because `from_white_alpha` is not `const`. The values are equal (ecolor 0.36.2); the test pins them against `from_white_alpha`.
- The colour-literal guard loses the rows of `ground_ink.rs` and `viewcube.rs`. `shell.rs` goes from 9 to 7. `theme/tables.rs` goes from 38 to 62.
- The example theme and the colour table of the user guide have the twelve keys.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1120-ground-inks.md`.

## Pinning tests

In `crates/ui/tests/theme_viewport_inks.rs`:

- `the_built_in_columns_keep_the_view_cube_and_marker_colours`: each table carries the old literals of its ground.
- `the_view_cube_inks_follow_the_viewport_ground_of_a_theme_file`: the ground rule, in the two directions, with a key that the file sets. This test fails when the rule is removed (checked locally).
- `each_view_cube_ink_is_a_theme_key`: each key sets its own ink.

Also: `theme_example::example_loads_and_holds_the_dark_defaults` (the example equals `Tokens::DARK`), the existing `viewport_ground_tests` (cube greys and 3:1 contrast on the light ground), and `colour_literals::no_colour_literal_outside_the_allowed_rows`.

## Gates

On the head 114f7b171:

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 12 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (2.3 min).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches none (0 steps reached).

## Not exercised

- No check by hand in the GUI and no screenshot. The tests pin the values.
- `shell.rs` has CRLF line ends. The commit keeps them; the diff of that file is two lines.

Changelog: Themes can set the view cube, nav button, corner hint, playback marker, axis and viewport hover colours. A theme that makes the 3D view light or dark gets the matching built-in set for each colour that it omits.

Refs #1120

title: refactor(ui): viewport handle and pick inks are theme tokens
body:
Stacked on #3990. This branch starts from `issue/1120-theme-colour-tokens` (the guard). Its own commit is the last one (55001e555). Review that commit; the two commits before it are #3990. Merge #3990 first.

## What changed

The first family of #1120: the viewport handle and pick inks.

- Three colour tokens join `Tokens` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme.rs`). Each is also a theme-file key (`colors.<name>`, `theme_files::COLOR_NAMES`):

  | Token | Draws | Was |
  |---|---|---|
  | `handle_shade` | the shadow under a move or turn handle and under its readout | `Color32::from_black_alpha(170)` |
  | `handle_text` | the readout text of a handle, and the fallback ink of an axis | `Color32::WHITE` |
  | `pick_rim` | the rim of a picked point's disc | `Color32::from_rgb(245, 240, 250)` |

- Both built-in tables (`theme/tables.rs`) carry the old values, so no pixel changes. The light table keeps the dark values: the handles and the picks draw over the 3D view, not over the chrome.
- The draw sites read `theme::current()`: `egui_app/move_handles.rs`, `egui_app/turn_handles.rs`, `align_pick_viz.rs`.
- The colour-literal guard (`crates/ui/tests/colour_literals.rs`) loses the rows of those three files. The row of `theme/tables.rs` goes from 32 to 38 (3 tokens in 2 tables).
- Wiring of the new keys: `theme_files/names.rs`, `theme_files/overlay.rs`, `assets/themes/theme.json.example`, and the colour table of `docs/user-guide/themes.md`.
- `geom_legal` and its two const asserts move unchanged from `theme.rs` (425 lines) to the new `theme/legal.rs`. `theme.rs` is now 318 lines.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1120-handle-inks.md` (flat names, the light column, what was dropped).

## Pinning tests

- `theme_viewport_inks::the_built_in_columns_keep_the_handle_and_pick_colours` (new file `crates/ui/tests/theme_viewport_inks.rs`): both columns carry the old literals.
- `theme_viewport_inks::a_theme_file_sets_each_handle_and_pick_ink_by_name`: a theme file sets the three keys, with no "unknown key" note.
- `theme_example::example_has_exactly_the_loader_keys`: the example file has the three new keys.
- `colour_literals::no_colour_literal_outside_the_allowed_rows`: the three files have no colour literal left.

## Gates

On the head 55001e555:

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 12 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (2.5 min). It includes `ui suites: lib`, `ui suites: colour_literals`, `ui suites: theme_example`, `ui suites: theme_files` and `ui suites: theme_viewport_inks`.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches none (`cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run`: 0 steps reached).

## Not exercised

- No check by hand in the GUI and no screenshot. The values are the old ones; the test pins them.
- The shipped themes `teal-night.json` and `horizon-day.json` do not set the new keys. They take the values of their base table, as before.

title: test(ui): guard against new colour literals outside the theme tokens
body:
## What changed

This is the first PR for #1120. It adds a guard and changes no colour.

- New test file `crates/ui/tests/colour_literals.rs`. It walks `crates/ui/src` and counts the colour literals in each file that is not a test file (`tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs`, `tests/`). A colour literal is a named constant such as `Color32::WHITE`, or a constructor whose arguments are all numbers written in place, such as `Color32::from_rgb(245, 240, 250)`, also across lines. A constructor over variables (`from_rgb(r, g, b)`) converts a colour chosen elsewhere and does not count. `Color32::TRANSPARENT` does not count. A line comment does not count.
- Each count must equal its row in `ALLOWED`:
  - a file with a new literal, or a file with no row, fails: "read a theme token instead";
  - a file with fewer literals fails until its row is lowered or removed. Thus the list only shrinks.
- Each row says why:
  - `keep:` for a colour that is not a choice for a theme: the token tables, the contrast maths, and a colour that only measures text;
  - `move (#1120 <family>)` for a site that a later PR moves to theme tokens.
- On `main` at f287a370c the list has 24 files and 142 literals. About 105 of them are sites to move (the 2026-11-12 estimate said 51).
- The guard does not see colour data kept as plain numbers: the G-code syntax table in `gcode_highlight.rs` (tuples) and `[u8; 3]` consts such as `PICK_RGB8`. The family PRs move those by name.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1120-colour-literal-guard.md`.

## The plan after this PR

One PR for each family. Each adds its tokens to `Tokens` (dark and light tables) and to the theme-file keys (`theme_files::COLOR_NAMES`), moves the sites, and lowers its rows. Each is `Refs #1120`. The last one is `Fixes #1120`.

1. Viewport overlays: pick, avoid and handle inks, ground ink, view cube, viewport bar, generate overlay, drop hint, shell overlays.
2. Tool drawings: tool, holder and profile previews, tool library views.
3. Verdict palettes (`colorvision.rs`): into the token table, values unchanged, as the issue says.
4. G-code syntax colours, window chrome and status inks.

## Pinning tests

- `colour_literals::no_colour_literal_outside_the_allowed_rows`: the guard. A failure prints today's counts in the row format.
  - With one literal added to `egui_app/error_text.rs`, it fails with `egui_app/error_text.rs: 2 colour literals, the row allows 1: read a theme token instead`.
  - With one `Color32::WHITE` in `egui_app/window_chrome.rs` replaced by `Color32::TRANSPARENT`, it fails with `egui_app/window_chrome.rs: 1 colour literals, the row says 2: lower the row to 1`.
- `colour_literals::the_rows_are_sorted_and_each_says_why`.
- `colour_literals::the_counter_sees_each_form_and_skips_comments`: the counter on a fixed text, with a constructor split over lines and two conversions of variables that must not count.

## Gates

On the head 7614c70db (two commits: the guard, then the stricter counter):

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 1 step (`ui suites: colour_literals`), 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps -p camcraft-ui --test colour_literals -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `rustfmt --check` on the new file: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches none (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: 0 steps reached).

## Not exercised

- No change to the app. The guard reads source files only.
- A literal written through a `use` alias (for example `use egui::Color32 as C`) is not counted. No such alias is in `crates/ui` today.

title: feat(ui): the 3D tool preview shows helical flutes
body:
## Why

The user asked to see the flutes in the 3D model preview. The maintainer wrote: "as long as we keep the 3D preview bit, im aiming to develop on that down the line / as running weirdly shape tools requires models / not just a spun profile".

## What changed

- The 3D preview of the tool library window cuts helical flute grooves into the fluted length of the revolved model (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library_dialog/flutes.rs`, new).
  - Count: the stated `flutes`, 1 to 16. No stated count gives no flutes.
  - Helix: `catalog.helix_deg`, 0 to 80 degrees. The value 0, no value, or a value out of range gives straight flutes. The helix is right-hand: the twist is `z * tan(helix) / R`.
  - Groove: a sine section on 45 % of each flute pitch. The floor is 60 % of the local radius, so a groove fades at a ball tip and at a drill point. The grooves run out over the top 8 % of the fluted length.
  - Kinds with flutes: end mill, ball nose, bull nose, twist drill, chamfer mill. All other kinds (tap, thread mills, form mill, T-slot, keyseat, dovetail, lollipop, turning, EDM, plasma, waterjet, wire, probe) show the plain model.
- A "Flutes" toggle follows "Dimensions" and "Holder" (view state, starts on). The toggle queues no command. The row can wrap in a narrow preview, and the drawing then takes the height that is left.
- `ToolModel` keeps `fluted` and `fluted_bare` next to the plain meshes. `ToolModel::shown(holder, flutes)` picks the mesh. The view box is the box of the plain mesh, so a toggle does not move the view.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3908-tool-preview-flutes.md`.

## Display-only rule (safety)

- The fluted mesh is built in a private module (`mod flutes`, not `pub`) of `crates/ui`. No crate below `ui` (app, sim, motion, post, tools) can name it.
- The steel outline, the holder bands of the collision check, the plain meshes, `Tool::geom` and `Tool::profile` do not change with the flutes. Pinned by `the_flutes_do_not_change_what_the_checks_read`.
- Each fluted point is on or inside the revolved envelope (a groove only removes radius). Pinned by `the_fluted_steel_stays_inside_the_revolved_envelope`.

## Triangle bound

96 facets around. The fluted length has 16 to 64 rings (one ring for each 0.12 rad of twist). A meridian with more than 120 points gets no flutes. The fluted steel has at most 2 * 96 * 119 = 22,848 facets. A `const` assertion checks that this is not more than the painted budget of the model view (`MAX_PAINTED` = 30,000), and the build refuses a larger mesh. Reading (computed from the rule, not measured): the seeded Ø 6 end mill with 4 flutes and a 30 degree helix has 24 rings and about 5,200 facets of fluted steel.

## Frame cost

The fluted meshes are built with the rest of the model, on the same key (the draft tool value, which holds `flutes` and the helix). A still frame builds nothing and projects nothing. A changed helix builds the model one time. The toggle builds nothing: it picks a mesh that is already built, and the projection cache projects the new pick one time.

## Pinning tests

- `flutes::tests::an_end_mill_shows_its_flute_count_on_the_fluted_length` (2, 3, 4 and 6 flutes; the groove floor is the core; the shank is plain)
- `flutes::tests::helix_zero_cuts_straight_grooves_and_a_helix_twists_them`
- `flutes::tests::the_fluted_steel_stays_inside_the_revolved_envelope`
- `flutes::tests::tools_without_flutes_draw_the_plain_model`
- `flutes::tests::the_fluted_steel_keeps_to_its_facet_bound`
- `tool_library_preview::the_flutes_toggle_shows_and_hides_the_helical_flutes` (no command, a plain model when off, the same holder)
- `tool_library_preview::the_flutes_do_not_change_what_the_checks_read`
- `tool_library_preview::a_changed_helix_rebuilds_the_fluted_model_once` (a still frame computes no mesh)
- `page_layout_tool_library::layout_window_tool_editor` (updated: Flutes follows Holder on its row or wraps under it, inside the window)

The ui lib `#[test]` count goes from 1656 to 1664 (8 new tests, none removed). No snapshot PNG changes. Each changed file has fewer than 400 lines.

## Gate (Windows, winbuild)

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head `a3dee508f` (log `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-3908-a3dee508f.log`, first line `HEAD: a3dee508f5dbb28025c09b507bbae5830fec7939`):

```
  ok     229s  ui build (--no-run)
  ok     121s  ui suites: lib
  ok  (16 more ui suites: boundary .. waterjet_tool, 1-3 s each)
  wall 6.6 min, 18 step(s), 0 failed, 0 stalled
```

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the same head: clean (exit 0). Only `camcraft-ui` changed.

## Not exercised

- The live app with a mouse (the screenshots come from the headless egui_kittest renderer).
- A tool with an imported body that is also fluted (the revolved steel below a body gets the flutes; the body is drawn as it is).
- No post, toolpath or check code changed, so no example catalog suite and no light lane apply.

## Screenshots

Holder off in each view, so that the cutter is larger. "Before" is main `10ea81a2a`; "after" is head `a3dee508f`.

| | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| End mill, 4 flutes, 30° | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3908/before-endmill-4fl-30deg.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3908/after-endmill-4fl-30deg.png) |
| Ball mill, 2 flutes, 30° | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3908/before-ballmill-2fl-30deg.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3908/after-ballmill-2fl-30deg.png) |

| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3908/after-endmill-4fl-helix0.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3908/after-endmill-flutes-off.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-3908/after-endmill-3fl-45deg-holder.png) |

title: fix(wire): join tangent arcs without zero-length connector moves
body:
## What changed

The wire contour of a drawn line-and-arc profile (#3937) moves each arc onto its lattice centre with its radius kept. Two neighbour arcs with different centres then end a small distance apart. Before this change, `stitch` in `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_cut.rs` wrote a connector line across that gap. The post rounded that line to the arc end, so each tangent joint gave a `G1` block with no motion.

The cause is in `stitch`: an arc followed by an arc with a different end always got a `Span::Line` joiner. In the test oval below, each joiner is about 5e-9 mm long.

## The rule

- Two neighbour arcs whose ends are no more than `JOIN_MAX` (2.5 um, ten times `JOINT_TOL`) apart meet at the mean of the two ends. No connector move is written.
- The rule applies only when the half gap is under a quarter of the chord of each arc. Then no end can pass the other, and no arc can read as a full circle.
- Each moved end stands up to half the gap off its circle. The path margin now adds that half gap (`arc_gaps`, measured on the snapped first walk). When the margin is not zero, the path has a note for the joint shift.
- The kerf and cover laws do not change. They read the recorded arcs, and they read an arc whose two end radii differ as the mean circle less half the difference. So they still check the exact drawing.
- A wider gap, or an arc too short for the rule, keeps a connector line. That line is a real move of more than 2.5 um.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3959-wire-arc-joins.md`.

## Readings

- Four-centre oval of tangent arcs (centres at (+-2 sqrt 2, 0) and (0, -+sqrt 3), no centre on the lattice), die, start hole at the origin. Before: 11 moves, of which 4 are connector lines of about 5e-9 mm. After: lead in, 5 arcs (the seam arc in two parts), lead out. The joint gaps are far under 1 nm, so the margin is zero and there is no margin note.
- The same oval with the top arc lifted by 100 nm (a drawing joint gap at its two ends): the arcs join directly. The margin is 150.2 nm (100 nm drawing gap, 50 nm joint shift, 0.2 nm centre snap), and the note says "up to 50.0 nm".
- The posted ISO program of the oval DXF: 5 `G3` blocks one after the other, no `G1` between them. Each motion block moves the wire by more than 1e-6 mm. Without the fix, this test fails with a `G1` block between two arcs.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib: `wire_edm::arc_tests::tangent_arcs_join_arc_to_arc_with_no_connector_move` (die and punch: no line between arcs, each move longer than the lattice, the moves chain, the kerf law passes; and an arc moved 2 um into the product still fails the kerf law).
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `wire_edm::arc_tests::tangent_arcs_across_a_joint_gap_meet_at_its_mean_and_the_margin_holds_it`.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_dxf_selection`: `arcs::tangent_arcs_post_arc_to_arc_with_no_block_that_stands_still` (posted ISO program).
- The existing arc tests and law tests stay green, also `the_laws_catch_a_mutated_arc_path`.

## Goldens moved

None. The goldens of #3937 (`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/{wire-iso,sodick-wire,g-edm}/wire_dxf_*`) have no arc-to-arc joint: the circle halves share their ends exactly, and in the punch each arc is between two lines. They stay byte-identical.

Effect on another PR: #3958 (DXF splines and ellipses) adds `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc` with 72 zero-length `G1` blocks. When #3958 and this PR are both on `main`, that golden loses those blocks. The PR that merges second regenerates it.

## Not exercised

- The Sodick and G-EDM posts with a tangent arc chain (the posted test uses the generic ISO post; the change is in the toolpath, before the post).
- A joint gap between `JOIN_MAX` and the walk's own limit. The walk does not make one today.

## Gate

All on head `c7894675f` (Mac, debug unless stated):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 23 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (2.7 min). It includes `motion suites: lib`, `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour` and `wire_dxf_selection (arcs::)`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light` (release): 6 steps, 0 failed.
- The pinning tests were red before the fix: the motion test found 4 connector lines of about 5e-9 mm; the posted test found a `G1` block between two `G3` blocks.

Heavy step: none. This PR is `P7`, so it gets no targeted heavy step ("Heavy lanes at review").

Changelog: Wire EDM: two tangent arcs of a drawn profile now join arc to arc; the program has no `G1` block with no motion between them.

title: fix(plasma): Plasma Profile takes a start pick and an exit pick
body:
## What changed

- Plasma Profile takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `Ring` (`KindInfo::pick()`).
- The picks are the operation-level `picks` of #3339 / PR #3871. This PR adds no field, no command and no MCP tool.
- Start pick: the lead-in of the nearest closed contour lands on the projection of the pick on the profile. The pierce is at the start of that lead-in, in the scrap.
- Exit pick: the torch cuts the full contour. Then it cuts on to the projection of the exit pick. The lead-out leaves there and the torch goes off at its end.
- Small-hole rule: the pierce stays at the centre and there is no lead-out. A start pick sets where the straight lead-in meets the hole. An exit pick sets where the torch goes off. It must be at or past the overburn.
- Each contour without a pick keeps its automatic seam.
- A pick that a law cannot hold is refused by name. It is never moved. The text names the role and the point:
  - a pick farther than 1.5 kerf widths from each closed profile;
  - a pick when the operation has open runs only;
  - a lead-in or a lead-out with no room beside the part at the pick (the pierce or the torch off would be on the part);
  - a small-hole lead-in from the centre that would cross the part;
  - a small-hole exit pick inside the overburn;
  - an exit pick with control compensation (G41/G42), at the command door and in the generator.
- The kerf law and the cover law still judge the complete path.
- New generator door: `camcraft_motion::plasma::plasma_profile_picked`. `plasma_profile` calls it with no pick.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Plasma Profile. The command refused each pick on the kind. The generator always chose the seam (`longest_mid`, or the point nearest the centre for a small hole).

## Where the issue is silent (smallest change taken)

- Which contour takes a pick: the closed contour whose profile is nearest. The reach is 1.5 kerf widths (the 2D contour uses 1.5 tool diameters).
- How the cut gets to the exit: a run past the start in the cut direction. The stretch between the start and the exit is cut two times. A note on the path gives its length.
- "After the overburn": only the small-hole rule has an overburn. There the exit must be at or past it. A contour with leads has no overburn, so the exit pick alone sets the run.
- An exit pick with G41/G42 is refused by name. The programmed contour ends at its start, and a longer one needs a new proof of the compensation span. Mutation M2 showed that the generator emits a path without that refusal.
- Waterjet: `WaterjetProfile` is on `main` now, with its own planner and tabs. This PR does not change it. A pick on it is still refused by name. The slice is #3983.
- UI: this PR changes no UI file. The operation page reads `KindInfo::pick()`.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/3334-plasma-start-exit.md`.

## Tests

Final head: `845228ac0`, on `upstream/main` `10ea81a2a`.

Pins (new):

- `camcraft-app`, `start_exit_shared` suite, submodule `start_exit_shared/plasma.rs` (7 tests):
  - `the_pierce_is_at_the_start_pick_and_the_torch_goes_off_at_the_exit_pick` (golden CL `plasma_start_exit_picks.cl`)
  - `a_pick_whose_pierce_falls_on_the_part_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pick_that_is_far_from_each_profile_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_small_hole_keeps_its_rule_under_the_picks`
  - `an_exit_pick_under_control_compensation_is_refused_at_the_door`
  - `undo_and_redo_restore_the_picks_and_the_path`
  - `the_plasma_profile_takes_a_start_pick_and_an_exit_pick`
- `camcraft-app`, `mcp_plasma`: `plasma_mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_start_and_exit_picks` (MCP `edit_operation` sets the picks, `generate` holds them, undo clears them, a far pick is refused by name).
- `camcraft-app`, `start_exit_shared`: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (extended: Plasma Profile is `Ring`).
- `camcraft-motion` lib, `plasma::picks_tests` (9 tests), with `no_pick_is_the_automatic_path_move_for_move`.

Red before the fix: I put the six source files of `upstream/main` back and ran the app pins. All 7 plasma pick tests failed, the MCP pin failed and the capability test failed (`left: NotTaken("the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships")`). With the fix, all pass.

Mutation results (one guard off for each run, then restored; each run was red, and green after the restore):

| # | Guard off | Red test |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | reach (`d > reach`) | `plasma::picks_tests::a_pick_that_no_law_can_hold_is_refused_by_name` |
| M2 | exit pick with control compensation (generator) | `plasma::picks_tests::control_compensation_holds_the_start_pick_and_refuses_the_exit_pick` |
| M3 | open runs take no pick | `plasma::picks_tests::a_pick_that_no_law_can_hold_is_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | `PathPicks::refusal` (two picks of a role, a pick that is not a number) | `plasma::picks_tests::a_pick_that_no_law_can_hold_is_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | small-hole lead-in across the part | `plasma::picks_tests::a_small_hole_lead_in_that_would_cross_the_part_is_refused_by_name` (the kerf law still refused the path, without the name of the pick) |
| M6 | small-hole exit inside the overburn | `plasma::picks_tests::a_small_hole_keeps_its_rule_and_its_overburn` |
| M7 | the name of the pick in the lead refusal | `a_pick_whose_pierce_falls_on_the_part_is_refused_by_name` |
| M8 | command door (`PlasmaOp::pick_refusal` in `sane.rs`) | `an_exit_pick_under_control_compensation_is_refused_at_the_door` |

Gates:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 762 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This run was on head `0d0945471` (base `97a676e5c`). It includes `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl`, the `camcraft-motion` lib and the `camcraft-ui` lib.
- Then `upstream/main` moved by 8 commits (PR #3957, the wire exit pick, changes `pick_kinds.rs` and `start_exit_shared.rs`). I rebased the branch (it was not pushed yet). There was no conflict. I moved the pin file into the `start_exit_shared` suite. The source files did not change after the full run.
- On the rebased tree I ran again: `motion suites: lib`, `ui suites: lib`, and the app suites `start_exit_shared`, `mcp_plasma`, `golden_cl`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `plasma_profile`, `plasma_gate`, `plasma_post`, `plasma_machine`, `plasma_cut_data`, `post_serves_plasma`, `coarse_probe_plasma`, `waterjet_profile`, `wire_contour`, `contour_start_point`, `cut_recipe`, `pick`, `project_roundtrip`. All passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the final head.
