title: fix(turning): Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish take a start and an exit pick
body:
Slice 1 of #3331: Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish. This PR does not close the issue. The eight other turning kinds are the next slices.

## Review fixes

Head: `449c54fd935d9dd7a6b0d800b6664542bd26ed70`.
Base: `upstream/main` at `baad348f191a5f2261dc778ac3f9853aaf19ffa0`.

- Both `.map_err(&refuse)` calls now use `.map_err(refuse)`.
- The branch includes a merge of current upstream main. The conflict resolutions keep both independent changes.
- `PickCapability::takes` keeps the upstream wire exit support and the new turning capability.
- The MCP description and the shared capability test keep the wire and turning changes.
- A second upstream refresh retains the new Slot `Ends` capability and the turning capability. The shared test keeps both assertions.
- The second refresh does not change the turning controls shown in the screenshots.
- The screenshots below show the old groups and the new turning controls.

## What changed

- A turning pick is a point in the lathe (Z, X) plane. It is a model point `[x, y, z]`. The planner reads it as (station, radius) about the fitted turning axis.
- Start: one rapid goes from the opening point of the path to the pick. The first feed starts at the pick and ends where it ended before.
- Exit: one feed goes from the end of the last feed to the pick. One rapid goes from the pick to the old end point of the path.
- The moves between the first feed and the last feed do not change.
- New module `crates/motion/src/turning/start_exit.rs` (`with_picks`, `PickLaw`). It works on the finished path of a kernel. The kernels do not change.
- The registry has a new capability, `PickCapability::Meridian`, for the three kinds.
- Threading says "not taken" with its own reason: "the thread start law sets the start and the exit of a thread". The G76 start judge does not change.
- MCP: the `edit_operation` schema names the three kinds and says that z is necessary. `list_operation_types` gives `start_exit.plane` for them.
- UI: the Geometry tab of the three kinds has a Start point group and an Exit point group. The rows are typed (Z and X). Apply uses `EditOperationParams`.

A pick is refused by name, and is never moved, when one of these is true:

- The pick has no Z (refused at the command door, with the name of the kind).
- The pick is not in air: it is inside the stock radius and behind the free end, each grown by the nose radius.
- The pick is on the chuck side of the bar.
- The rapid to the start, or the rapid from the exit, crosses the stock envelope.
- The feed between the pick and the cut comes nearer to the part than nose radius + stock to leave - tolerance.
- The exit feed runs along the surface that the last pass cut.
- The path has canned cycles or control compensation.

## Cause

The turning kinds had the `picks` field of #3339, but no planner read it. The registry gave each turning kind the "owed" reason, so the command door refused each pick.

## Where the issue is silent

- The issue does not say how the tool gets from the pick to the first pass. I chose the smallest change: the first feed of the kernel starts at the pick. The kernel ladder does not change.
- The issue does not say which stock a rapid must miss. I chose the envelope of the part and the setup stock. It does not follow stock that earlier operations removed. This is the safe side.
- The issue does not ask for a viewport pick. A turning point is in air, so the wall snap of the 2D Contour pick is not correct for it. The rows are typed.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/3331-turning-start-exit.md`.

## Tests

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared/turning.rs` (8 tests, in the existing `start_exit_shared` binary):
  - `the_first_pass_starts_at_the_start_pick`
  - `the_last_pass_leaves_at_the_exit_pick`
  - `a_start_and_an_exit_pick_hold_together`
  - `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pick_whose_move_crosses_the_part_or_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`
  - `threading_keeps_its_start_law_and_says_so_by_name`
  - `undo_and_redo_restore_the_path`
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_turning_picks_and_undo_clears_them`
- `crates/motion/src/turning/start_exit_tests.rs` (8 unit tests, `turning::start_exit::tests::*`).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turning_start_exit_tests.rs` (4 tests, `egui_app::turning_start_exit_rows::tests::*`).
- `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` now includes the new capability (an expected change of a pinned list).

Original implementation pin proof: each guard was removed, the pin failed, and the guard was restored.

| Guard removed | Result | Red test |
|---|---|---|
| `generate.rs` of `upstream/main` (no pick laid) | red | 6 of the 8 app tests: `the_first_pass_starts_at_the_start_pick`, `the_last_pass_leaves_at_the_exit_pick`, `a_start_and_an_exit_pick_hold_together`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name`, `a_pick_whose_move_crosses_the_part_or_the_stock_is_refused_by_name`, `undo_and_redo_restore_the_path` |

title: fix(sinker): Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn take a start and an exit pick
body:
## What changed

- The Sinker Burn takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `PickCapability::Ring`: the ring is its orbit.
  - A pick is an angle round the burn position (`x`, `y`). The start pick is where the orbit starts. The exit pick is where the orbit ends.
  - Circular: the circle starts at the start angle and makes one full turn counter-clockwise. With an exit pick it continues to the exit angle.
  - Planetary: the spiral turns from the start angle and reaches the radius there. The closing circle starts there.
  - Vector: the vector toward the start pick is burned first. The vector toward the exit pick is burned last.
  - After the exit angle the electrode feeds back to the burn position and retracts up the burn axis, as before.
- The Sinker Side Burn takes a start pick and an exit pick. Its pick capability is `PickCapability::Ends`.
  - The side move has two ends: the burn position and the wall end (the burn position moved by `amount` toward the wall).
  - A pick on the wall side of the middle of the move chooses the wall end. A pick on the other side chooses the burn position.
  - The start pick chooses the end where the electrode plunges. The exit pick chooses the end where it retracts.
- These picks are refused by name, at the command door and at generation. No pick is moved.
  - A pick on a Sinker Burn without an orbit: `Sinker Burn: a start point is not taken without an orbit - a straight plunge starts and ends at the burn position; ...`.
  - A pick on the burn position: it gives the orbit no angle.
  - A pick between two vectors of a vector orbit: `... is on no vector of the orbit ...`.
  - An exit vector that the vector order cannot end on.
  - A side burn pick at the middle of the side move: it chooses no end.
- With no pick each generator calls the earlier function. Each path without a pick is byte-identical.
- A path with a pick has one more note. The note names the start point and the exit point.
- The Geometry tab of each kind has a "Start point" group and an "Exit point" group with typed X and Y rows. A Sinker Burn without an orbit shows "Not taken - a straight plunge starts and ends at the burn position; state an orbit on the Passes tab".
- The schema text of MCP `edit_operation` names the two kinds. `list_operation_types` answers `start_exit: { start: true, exit: true, field: "picks" }` for them.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn. The door refused each pick. `sinker_orbit::orbit_offsets` always started the orbit at +X. `sinker_side::side_burn_worn` always plunged and retracted at the burn position.

## Design

The issue is exact about what each pick sets. Where it is silent, I took the smallest change. The decision file is `docs/decisions/3333-sinker-start-exit.md`.

- **The laws hold at each angle.** A circle keeps its own vertices, and the start and the exit are added vertices. The four axis directions stay vertices, so the walls move out by exactly the radius. Each vertex is on or inside the radius (`sinker_orbit::on_disc`). The undersize law and the cavity limits (`cavity_x`, `cavity_y`) count the radius, so they hold. A vector orbit keeps its directions; a pick changes the order only.
- **The orbit returns to the burn position before the retract.** The layered burn plunges each layer on the burn axis, so the orbit must end there between two layers. The retract law is not changed. The issue says "where the orbit ends before the retract": the last position on the radius is the exit angle.
- **The side burn's ends.** The issue says "the side where the side move begins". I read "side" as an end of the move. The `direction` parameter stays the one input for the wall. The electrode is at the same two positions at the same tip for each choice, so the burned volume is the same. `side_burn_worn` runs first, so the allowance law, the wear law and the layer law refuse before a pick is read.
- **No new field.** The picked generators take the ends as an argument: `sinker_wear::burn_compensated_between` and `sinker_picks::side_burn_between`. `SinkerParams` and `Orbit` are not changed.
- **No new command and no new file key.** The picks use the existing `EditOperationParams` and the `picks` field of #3339. The stamp already includes the picks.
- The new code is in one motion module, `crates/motion/src/sinker_picks.rs`. The UI rows are in one new file, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/sinker_pick_rows.rs`.

## Tests

Pins in the `start_exit_shared` suite of `camcraft-app` (`crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared/sinker.rs` and `sinker_side.rs`). Each name below has the prefix `sinker::`. The first seven were red before the fix, on unchanged `upstream/main` code at `707dac12a`. No new test binary is added.

- `a_circular_orbit_starts_at_the_start_pick_and_ends_at_the_exit_pick` (also: no gouge in `simulate_document`; a start at +X gives the automatic moves; undo and redo restore the previous path)
- `a_planetary_orbit_reaches_its_radius_at_the_start_pick`
- `a_vector_orbit_starts_on_the_picked_vector_and_ends_on_the_exit_vector`
- `a_pick_that_the_orbit_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
- `side::a_side_burn_starts_and_ends_at_the_picked_ends_of_its_side_move` (five choices of ends; the wall position in the stock sim; no gouge; undo and redo restore the previous path)
- `side::a_side_burn_pick_at_the_middle_of_the_move_is_refused_by_name`
- `side::mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_sinker_picks_and_refuses_an_impossible_one_by_name`
- `side::the_generator_refuses_an_impossible_sinker_pick_by_name` (added with the fix; it calls `operation::generate` directly)
- `a_picked_orbit_keeps_the_undersize_law_and_the_cavity_limits` (added with the fix; a rough pass with a pick generates inside the radius, and an orbit past the cavity is refused by the undersize law)

More tests:

- `camcraft-motion` lib: `sinker_picks::tests::*` (7 tests: the automatic orbit is unchanged; each picked orbit stays inside its radius and keeps the axis vertices and each circle vertex; the vector order; the refusals; a layered worn burn; the side ends; the side burn keeps each refusal).
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::sinker_pick_rows::tests::*` (3 tests: labels, switches, the seeded draft, the "Not taken" line).

Red before the fix: the pins that existed then (the first six of the list, and after it the MCP pin) failed with `Sinker Burn: a start point is not taken - the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships; clear it on this operation` (or the same text for `Sinker Side Burn`).

Mutation results (old code back, pins run, fix restored):

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| `pick_kinds.rs` from `upstream/main` | the first seven app pins (all that set a pick through the command door) |
| `pick_kinds.rs`: the door check of the two kinds removed | `a_pick_that_the_orbit_cannot_hold_...`, `side::a_side_burn_pick_at_the_middle_...`, `side::mcp_edit_operation_sets_...` |
| `sinker_op.rs` from `upstream/main` | the circular, planetary and vector pins, `side::the_generator_refuses_...` |
| `sinker_side_op.rs` from `upstream/main` | `side::a_side_burn_starts_and_ends_...`, `side::the_generator_refuses_...` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "no orbit" guard off | `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_reads_angles_and_refuses_by_name` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "on the burn position" guard off | `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_reads_angles_and_refuses_by_name` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "on no vector" guard off | `sinker_picks_a_vector_orbit_keeps_its_directions_in_the_picked_order`, `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_...` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the exit order guard off | `sinker_picks_orbit_ends_reads_angles_and_refuses_by_name` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the "middle of the side move" guard off | `sinker_picks_side_ends_choose_the_nearer_end_and_refuse_the_middle` |
| `sinker_picks.rs`: the circle makes half a turn | `sinker_picks_every_picked_orbit_stays_inside_its_radius_and_keeps_the_axis_vertices` |

All pins are green with the fix restored. The mutations ran on the same source code, before the pins moved into the `start_exit_shared` suite and before the ninth pin was added. The ninth pin was not in a mutation run.

Expected-change test: `start_exit_shared::every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` pinned "only the contour and the wire take a pick". It now names Sinker Burn as `Ring` and Sinker Side Burn as `Ends`.

## Review fixes

title: fix(slot): a Slot takes a start point and an exit point
body:
First slice of #3325: the Slot kind. The other kinds of the table stay refused by name.

## What changed

- A Slot takes a start point and an exit point (`PickCapability::Ends`).
- A start pick chooses the slot end where the pass starts. The cutter goes down at that end.
- An exit pick chooses the slot end where the pass stops.
- New planner `machining2d::slot_picked_ends` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_picks.rs`). It returns `(a, b)` or `(b, a)`. It does nothing else.
- The Slot arm of `generate.rs` calls the planner after `slot_extended_ends`, then calls `slot` as before.
- The Slot's Lead in / Lead out tab draws the Start point and Exit point groups. The viewport pick and the viewport marks take the Slot.
- MCP: `edit_operation` sets `picks` on a Slot (the field of #3339). `list_operation_types` answers `start: true, exit: true` for the Slot.

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for the Slot, so `sane.rs` refused each pick. The slot planner did not read a pick.

## Design (where the issue is silent, the smallest change)

- A pick only swaps the two ends. `slot(b, a)` is `slot(a, b)` turned half a turn about the middle of the slot. A half turn keeps the stadium, the rows, the wall lap and the climb sense. No new move shape is made. The test `a_swap_is_the_same_pass_turned_half_a_turn` proves this move by move, arcs included.
- Without a pick the planner returns its input. Each earlier slot is the same to the byte.
- Exit: the row count decides where a pass stops. An odd count stops at the end opposite the start. An even count stops at the end where it started (the wall lap of #2906 closes there). The issue says "the other end" for the exit. That holds for an odd count. For an even count the exit is at the start end, and a pick at the other end is refused by name.
- A start pick and an exit pick together: the start decides. An exit pick at the end where the pass does not stop is refused by name. The refusal gives the two ends and the row count.
- An exit pick alone turns the pass so that it stops at the nearest end.
- Reach: a pick farther from the cutter path than `1.5 x tool diameter + stock to leave` is refused by name. This is the contour's law (`contour_start.rs` `reach`). The cutter path is the stadium of the rows. A pick beside the middle of a long slot is in reach and takes the nearest end.
- A pick the same distance from both ends is refused by name. It names no end.
- A tilted (3+2) slot refuses a pick by name, as the tilted contour does. A pick is a model-frame point.
- The end extensions keep their ends: `extend_start` stays on `a`, `extend_end` on `b`. The #1504 room judges the authored slot as before.
- Entry law, first traverse and the keep-stock check judge the result as before. The start end already changed with the climb flag, so a start at either end is a pass that the generator made before this change.
- `docs/decisions/3325-slot-start-exit.md` has the full record.

## Tests

New test binary reasons:

- `crates/motion/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` groups the Slot end-selection and row-parity laws; no Slot directory suite exists.
- `crates/app/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` groups the Slot command, project-file, MCP, and generation checks; no Slot directory suite exists.

Pins:

- `crates/motion/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` (7 tests, new): `no_pick_is_the_earlier_slot`, `a_swap_is_the_same_pass_turned_half_a_turn`, `the_entry_is_at_the_end_nearest_the_start_pick`, `the_exit_is_at_the_end_nearest_the_exit_pick`, `both_picks_hold_or_the_exit_is_refused_by_name`, `a_pick_that_names_no_end_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_that_cannot_be_cut_keeps_its_own_refusal_under_a_pick`. They run one row, three rows and two rows, each with climb and with conventional.
- `crates/app/tests/slot_start_exit.rs` (6 tests, new): capability, entry at the pick, exit at the pick, refusals by name (impossible exit, out of reach, the middle, a tilted slot), command + undo + redo + project file + stamp, MCP `edit_operation` and `list_operation_types`.
- `crates/ui`: `the_slot_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_and_takes_a_start` (page, Apply, undo) and `a_slot_takes_the_viewport_pick_and_shows_its_marks`.
- `crates/app/tests/start_exit_shared.rs`: the capability list now expects `Ends` for the Slot (an expected change).

Red before the fix: the 6 app tests failed on unchanged `upstream/main` (`ddee3aed6`). Each failed with "Slot: a start point is not taken ..." or with `NotTaken` in place of `Ends`.

Mutations (each one applied, pin run, then restored; all green after the restore):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `generate.rs` from `upstream/main` (the planner does not read the picks) | RED: 4 app tests |
| the swap removed (`(from, to) = (a, b)`) | RED: 3 motion tests |
| the exit refusal removed | RED: `both_picks_hold_or_the_exit_is_refused_by_name` |
| the reach refusal removed | RED: `a_pick_that_names_no_end_is_refused_by_name` |
| the tie refusal removed | RED: `a_pick_that_names_no_end_is_refused_by_name` |
| the row parity removed (`stops_at_a = !climb`) | RED: 2 motion tests |
| `PathPicks::refusal` not read | RED: `a_pick_that_names_no_end_is_refused_by_name` |
| the tilted slot refusal removed | RED: `a_pick_the_pass_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name` |

Gates on the final head, against `upstream/main` `ddee3aed6`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `82251e67c` (this branch with `upstream/main` `d94b9816d` merged in): 303 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 47.7 min. It ran the `camcraft-ui` lib tests, `example_catalog`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens` and each `slot_*` suite.
- The same quick gate on the head before the merge (`9c08b726f`, base `ddee3aed6`): 303 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on `82251e67c`: 106 steps, 1 failed. The failed test is `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`, with the counts `(4688, 4660, 1980)`. Issue #3886 records this test red on main with the same counts. It is a 3D Pocket test. This PR changes only the Slot arm.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `c94dbe366`: clean.
- The final head `c94dbe366` adds one commit after the gated head. It collapses a nested `if` for clippy and does not change behaviour. On `c94dbe366` these ran again and passed: motion `slot_start_exit` (7) and `slot_round_ends` (4), app `slot_start_exit` (6), `start_exit_shared` (4), `slot_extension` (5), `example_catalog` (43). The full quick gate and the heavy lanes did not run again on `c94dbe366`.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples/catalog` is empty on the final head. `example_catalog`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens` and the slot suites ran and passed without a change. A slot without a pick gets its ends back as they are.

## UI

The Slot page, Lead in / Lead out tab (rendered from the real page code with `egui_kittest`):

| Before (`upstream/main`) | After, both points off | After, a start point set |
|---|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1eb1d0af49feee812dddf558e48d5905af2f700b/pr-3978/slot-leads-before-off.png) | ![after off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1eb1d0af49feee812dddf558e48d5905af2f700b/pr-3978/slot-leads-after-off.png) | ![after start set](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1eb1d0af49feee812dddf558e48d5905af2f700b/pr-3978/slot-leads-after-start-set.png) |

The images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch only. The third image shows the gap that "Not exercised" describes.

## Not exercised

- No run on a machine. No simulation of a picked slot against a part model: the swap gives a pass that the generator already made for the other climb sense, and the gouge laws judge it as before.
- Helix and ramp entries with a pick have no pin of their own. The entry certificate is the same stadium for both end orders (the half turn law).
- The Trochoidal Slot, Pocket, 2D Offset, Circular, Trace, Engrave and 2D Chamfer take no pick yet. Each is a later slice of #3325.
- The sentence in the `edit_operation` schema that lists the kinds is not changed. PR #3957 changes the next line, and an edit there makes a merge conflict. `list_operation_types` is the stated source and it names the Slot.
- No row in the `camcraft-mcp` skill (a process file).
- Seen during the screenshots, not changed here: in the `egui_kittest` page harness, a Start point group that is switched on puts its Clear button at the middle of the remaining page height. The rows below it (the consequence line and the Exit point group) are then below the page. The 2D Contour page on `upstream/main` shows the same in the same harness, so this is not from this PR. It is not known if the scrolling pane of the app shows it.

## Overlaps

- #3957 (Wire Contour exit pick) changes other lines of `pick_kinds.rs` (`takes`, the tail of `pick_refusal`) and of `start_exit_shared.rs`. A trial merge of this head with #3957 (`git merge-tree`) is clean.
- #3899, #3832, #3674, #3251, #3103 change other arms of `run_job_arms` in `generate.rs`, not the Slot arm. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3899, #3251 and #3103 also change `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs` or a UI start / exit file. This PR adds two lines to `mod.rs` and no trial merge with those three ran.

Changelog: A Slot takes a start point and an exit point: the pass starts at the slot end nearest the start point and stops at the end nearest the exit point, or the operation is refused by name.

Effort: high

## Review fix round

The Slot yaw transform now rotates temporary start and exit picks with the endpoints.
The stored model coordinates do not change.
The Trochoidal Slot arm keeps its previous transform.

The application pins cover start and exit picks at 90 and 180 degrees.
Each pin also checks a translated work offset and the stored model coordinates.

- `the_start_pick_holds_under_90_degree_wcs_yaw`
- `the_start_pick_holds_under_180_degree_wcs_yaw`
- `the_exit_pick_holds_under_90_degree_wcs_yaw`
- `the_exit_pick_holds_under_180_degree_wcs_yaw`

The two new integration binaries have their required reasons in the Tests section above.
No UI code, recorded program, snapshot, or process file changes in this round.
The UI images above remain applicable.

Pin proof: `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test slot_start_exit wcs_yaw -- --nocapture` ran twice.
With the source fix removed, all four yaw pins failed.
At 90 degrees, valid picks were refused as 15 mm from the cutter path, beyond the 9 mm reach.
At 180 degrees, the first descent and exit were at the opposite model endpoints.
After restoration, all four pins passed, including their translated-offset and stored-coordinate checks.

Final source head: `933847f5b8faa90fa93223c13ae1e6e5d22c98eb`.

I reran both gate plans with `--base upstream/main --dry-run` after that fetch.

title: perf(sim): section a prismatic Z slab once for a ramped path
body:
## What changed

The verifier shares model sections for geometric queries inside prismatic Z slabs of a ramped path.
A flat cut plane keeps its own section. A sloped wall keeps the plane-by-plane reading.

Law (c) keeps the exact boundary samples from every cut plane.
A shared geometric region does not prove that one sampled section covers every old collision sample.
The fallback sections each shared plane for the reach samples.
It keeps the original vertices, midpoints, and nudges.
It applies to small bands, near-tangent contacts, and large wall perimeters.
The fixed-spacing wall sample replacement is removed.

Law (b) asks the distance test before `edge_is_wall`.
These pure tests give the same result in either order.
The wall probe moves to `verify/section/wall.rs`.
The verifier reads the path. It does not change the moves or the posted program.

## Review finding

The previous wall sample replacement lost collision coverage.
The review reproduced zero warnings where the plane-exact reading found 500 `ShankHit` warnings.
The shank met stock above the finished part. The solid law could not replace that stock check.
Other cases lost findings with a small shank and a near-tangent contact.

The corrected law (c) keeps all original samples through the plane-exact fallback.
No fixed sample step is used as a proof of coverage.
Read `docs/decisions/3831-verify-keepdown-speed.md` for the decision.

## Performance limits

The previous 282 s to 1.2 s result used the unsafe sample replacement.
It does not describe this corrected implementation.
The fallback restores plane section work and the pooled samples for law (c).
The corrected implementation has not been timed on the earlier 38,432-facet plate.

## Tests and pin proof

The exported verifier has three new pins:

- `verify::slab_tests::a_shared_slab_keeps_near_tangent_stock_collisions`
- `verify::slab_tests::a_shared_slab_keeps_small_band_stock_collisions`
- `verify::slab_tests::a_shared_slab_keeps_stock_collisions_when_wall_spacing_would_widen`

Each pin expects 500 stock collision findings. All three pass with the fix.
`cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib verify::`: 182 passed.

Mutation proof: restore the reviewed sample replacement and run the three pins.
All three fail: each reports 0 findings against the expected 500.
Restore the plane-exact fallback and run the verifier tests again: 182 pass.
The mutation was removed before the final commit.

## Validation

Final head: `d8700760c03683818adf67cd50fabb5a8c2b3cd9`. Base: current `upstream/main` `97a676e5c2307f7a2bc3c7677d1cbe334df8ef40`.
Host: macOS arm64.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`): 133 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. Sim lib: 265 passed, including the three new pins.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`): 106 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled. The failed step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`. The test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` gives planner counts `(4688, 4660, 1980)` against `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. These are the same counts recorded before this fix round for issue #3886. I did not run this test on bare main. The isolated known-failure steps fail as expected and count as passed in the gate.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -j 4 -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `app suites: example_catalog`: the quick gate ran `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-app --no-fail-fast --test example_catalog -- --test-threads=4`. Result: 43 passed, 4 ignored.
- `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive` and `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4 cargo xtask gate batch --only "app suites: example_catalog_adaptive" --only "app suites: example_catalog_edge_work"`. Result: 2 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `app suites: solid_law_goldens`: the quick gate ran `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-app --no-fail-fast --test solid_law_goldens -- --test-threads=4`. Result: 7 passed.

The first quick runs stopped at a build cache fault (`E0463`) after target seeding.
The retry with four jobs gave the same fault.
I removed only the affected local package artifacts and ran the gate again.
The complete 133-step run then passed. No source change was needed.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog suites and `solid_law_goldens` passed without updates.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "examples/catalog"` is empty.
No recorded program changed.

## Not exercised

- The reporter's STEP model. It is not attached to the issue.
- Timings on the earlier plate with 16 holes.
- Windows and Linux.
- A lower move count for keep-down ramps. That changes posted G-code and is outside this PR.
- UI screenshots. No UI file changes.

Changelog: The verifier shares prismatic model sections for geometric queries and skips distant wall probes. Collision reach checks keep the exact samples from every cut plane.

Effort: high

Fixes #3831

title: fix(mcp): a pre-hello client cannot hold the ui link session
body:
## What changed

The UI link served one client at a time, and the token check only ran
when a complete line arrived. A local client without the token could
connect, send no newline, and hold the only session for the 5-minute
`IDLE_TIMEOUT`, blocking `camcraft-cli --ui`, while the app buffered up
to 16 MiB (`MAX_LINE`) for it.

Two new named constants in `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`:

- `PRE_HELLO_DEADLINE`: 5 s. A client that has not sent its hello line
  within 5 s of connecting is closed. The server writes its warning
  note ("no hello line in Ns") before the drop.
- `PRE_HELLO_MAX_LINE`: 4 KiB. The buffered-bytes cap before the token
  check; the drop message stays the existing "message too long" line.

In `serve_client`, the effective idle window is `idle.min(PRE_HELLO_DEADLINE)`
while the gate (the token) is still set, and the room computation and the
post-read cap check use the pre-hello cap until then. After the hello
passes, the 5-minute `IDLE_TIMEOUT` and the 16 MiB `MAX_LINE` apply as
before. No behaviour changes for `Inbox::listen` (no token, gate never
set) or for the in-process channel.

The busy test's client 1 in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` used
to simulate a slow call by connecting and staying silent - under the fix
that client is dropped after 5 s, so it now sends a real hello line and
holds the session like a served call. Its asserted behaviour (a second
call exits 4, busy) is unchanged.

## The pin

`a_client_that_sends_no_hello_cannot_hold_the_session`
(`crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`): client 1 connects and sends
nothing. Client 2, with the token, retries `link_call` (the link gives
up exit 4 while the session is held) and is served within seconds - the
whole test finishes in about 5.6 s. Without the pre-hello deadline the
silent client holds the session for 5 minutes, the retry bound expires,
and the test fails.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live ui_link`: 7 passed, 0 failed (5.3 s)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 307 passed, 0 failed (36.8 s)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## What was not exercised

- The Unix-socket transport path of the link (tests run on Windows TCP;
  the unix arms compile but were not run here).
- A client that trickles hello bytes past 4 KiB without a newline is
  covered by the same cap check, but only the no-hello path is pinned
  by a test.
- No real `camcraft-cli` binary run against a silent holder beyond what
  the existing busy test does.

Changelog: `camcraft-cli --ui` is no longer blockable for 5 minutes by a
local process that opens the link port and sends nothing.

Fixes #3873

title: fix(mcp): the cli talks only to the window that proves the token
body:
## What changed

#3874 asked the CLI to talk only to the real window. The first cut answered with a token-proof exchange; mkinney's review showed that exchange cannot work: the hello gives the token to the very peer it tries to check, so a false server that never read the discovery file still receives it and can compute the proof. This cut replaces it with a transport that verifies the peer.

- **Windows**: the window listens on a named pipe `\\.\pipe\camcraft-ui-link-<pid>` with a security descriptor that admits the window's own user only. The CLI asks the kernel which process serves the pipe (`GetNamedPipeServerProcessId`) and refuses a peer that is not the process the discovery file names - before one byte of the token crosses. The nonce/proof exchange is removed. A `"tcp"` entry is refused by name on every platform, with the risk in the diagnostic; this build never dials one.
- **Unix** keeps the 0700 socket folder; the review's read of the issue is that the risk does not occur there.
- **One hello deadline**: the connect, the hello write and the answer read run under one elapsed clock; a peer that trickles bytes ends within it (exit 4).
- **Bounded lines**: a line that reaches the 1 MiB bound without its newline closes the link; no remainder of an oversized line is parsed as a new message.
- **Bounded bridge**: reaching the bridge's copy bound with the session still open is a visible failure (exit 1), never a quiet success after a truncated answer.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/3874-ui-link-transport.md`.

## Dependency decision the maintainer must make

The PR declares two dependencies the maintainer has to confirm (both are already in `Cargo.lock` through other deps; no new crate):

- `windows-sys` on Windows: the pid-alive check (`OpenProcess`) and the named-pipe transport itself (`CreateNamedPipeW`, `ConnectNamedPipe`, `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId`, the SDDL user-only descriptor). A named pipe needs it - std has no pipe API; the `interprocess` crate is not in the lock and would be a new-crate decision. Features: `Win32_Foundation`, `Win32_System_Threading`, `Win32_System_IO`, `Win32_System_Pipes`, `Win32_Storage_FileSystem`, `Win32_Security`, `Win32_Security_Authorization`.
- `libc` on Unix: the pid-alive check through `kill(0)`.

## Readings (final head)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live ui_link`: 11 passed - the false-pipe pin (a pipe served by another process receives nothing: no token, no tool call), the TCP-refused pin, the slow-peer deadline, the oversized line with and without a final newline, the bridge bound, the busy exit 4, the wrong token, the stale-file removal.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live` (full binary): 25 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 307 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The pipe transport on Unix (the pipe code is `cfg(windows)`); the Unix path keeps the socket transport and its tests.
- A second local user is not emulated; the pipe's user-only ACL is kernel-enforced, and the CLI-side proof is the kernel-reported server process id.

Changelog: `camcraft-cli --ui` talks to the window over a named pipe with a user-only ACL on Windows (a TCP link address is refused), under one hello deadline, with capped answer lines and a bridge bound that reports a truncated session.

Fixes #3874

title: fix(drilling): Drill, Bore and Thread take a start and an exit pick as the hole order
body:
## What changed

- Drill, Bore and Thread (mill) take a start pick and an exit pick. Their pick capability is `PickCapability::HoleOrder`.
- The hole under the start pick is cut first. The hole under the exit pick is cut last.
- The holes between keep the list order, rotated to the start hole. Example, list A B C D: start C gives C D A B. Exit B gives A C D B. Start C with exit D gives C A B D.
- A pick is on a hole when it is inside the circle of the hole. The nearer centre wins when two circles hold the pick.
- With no pick, the hole list is not changed. Each program without a pick is byte-identical.
- These picks are refused by name. No pick is moved to a different hole.
  - A pick that is on no hole: `Drill: the start point (40.000, 30.000) is not on a hole of this operation - ...`.
  - A start pick and an exit pick on the same hole, when the list has more than one hole.
  - A pick on a Drill with cross holes.
  - A pick on a lathe's axial Drill (refused in the generator, because it needs the machine).
- The operation page of the three kinds has typed rows: "First hole stated", "First hole X / Y", "Last hole stated", "Last hole X / Y". A group that is switched on seeds the first (or the last) hole of the list.
- The schema text of MCP `edit_operation` names the three kinds. `list_operation_types` answers `start_exit: { start: true, exit: true, field: "picks" }` for them.
- Probe is not changed. Its row says "Not taken - a probe touches the part and cuts no path".

## Cause

`KindInfo::pick()` answered `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for Drill, Bore and Thread. The door refused each pick. The three arms of `generate` gave the hole list to the kernel in the list order (`drilling::drill`, `machining2d::bore_started`, `machining2d::thread_mill`). A direct `operation::generate` call ignored the picks without a note.

## Design

The issue and #3324 name the capability, the refusals and the example rule "the list order, rotated to the start". Where they are silent, I took the smallest change:

- "Near a hole" is "inside the circle of the hole". A search distance is not used.
- The rule is one function, `camcraft_motion::drilling::hole_order` (new module `drilling/order.rs`). The three arms of `generate` put the hole list in that order before the kernel reads it. The three kernels are not changed.
- The lathe's axial and cross holes refuse a pick. No XY order exists there.
- The picks ride the existing `EditOperationParams` and the existing `picks` field of #3339. No new command and no new file key.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/3328-drilling-hole-order.md`.

## Tests

Pins (all red before the fix, on unchanged `upstream/main` code at `ddee3aed6`):

- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::drill_cuts_the_picked_first_hole_and_last_hole` (golden `hole_order_drill.cl`)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::bore_cuts_the_picked_first_hole_and_last_hole` (golden `hole_order_bore.cl`)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::thread_cuts_the_picked_first_hole_and_last_hole_and_undo_restores_the_order` (golden `hole_order_thread.cl`; undo and redo of `EditOperationParams`)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::a_pick_that_is_not_on_a_hole_is_refused_by_name` (the three kinds; the door and the generator; two picks on one hole)
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::a_pick_on_a_drill_with_cross_holes_is_refused_by_name`
- `start_exit_shared::hole_order::mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_hole_order_picks_and_undo_clears_them`
- `drilling_axial::a_start_or_exit_pick_on_the_axial_hole_refuses_by_name`
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::start_exit_rows::tests::the_hole_kinds_type_their_first_and_last_hole`
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `drilling::order::tests::*` (4 tests of the rule)

Red before the fix: the six `hole_order` pins failed. The order pins read `[20, 60, 100, 140]` (the list order). The other pins read `Drill: a start point is not taken - the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships`.

Mutation results (old code back, pin run, fix restored):

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| `generate.rs` from `upstream/main` | `drill_cuts_...`, `bore_cuts_...`, `thread_cuts_...`, `a_pick_that_is_not_on_a_hole_...` (the generator check), `a_start_or_exit_pick_on_the_axial_hole_...` |
| `pick_kinds.rs`: the door check `hole_order().err()` removed, the cross-hole guard off | `a_pick_that_is_not_on_a_hole_...`, `a_pick_on_a_drill_with_cross_holes_...`, `mcp_edit_operation_sets_...` |
| `op_page.rs` from `upstream/main` | `the_hole_kinds_type_their_first_and_last_hole` |

All pins are green with the fix restored.

Expected-change test: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` pinned "only the contour and the wire take a pick". It now names the three hole kinds as `HoleOrder`.

Gates on head `5ad46c819` (base `ddee3aed6`):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 771 steps, 770 ok, 1 failed, 0 stalled, 89.8 min. The red step is `app suites: cadmpeg_import` (`stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed`). It is a time-limit test and this diff does not reach it. I ran `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test cadmpeg_import` alone after the gate: 13 passed, 0 failed.
- The quick plan included `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens`: all ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 11.8 min (release).

## Before and after UI screenshots

The page is the operation page on the tab that holds the Start point and Exit point groups. That tab is Geometry for Drill and Thread. It is "Lead in / Lead out" for Bore.

| Kind | Before (`ddee3aed6`, the merge base) | After (`5ad46c819`), groups off | After (`5ad46c819`), groups on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drill | ![Drill before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/before-drill.png) | ![Drill after, groups off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/after-drill-off.png) | ![Drill after, groups on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/after-drill-on.png) |
| Bore | ![Bore before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/before-bore.png) | ![Bore after, groups off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/after-bore-off.png) | ![Bore after, groups on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/after-bore-on.png) |
| Thread | ![Thread before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/before-thread.png) | ![Thread after, groups off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/after-thread-off.png) | ![Thread after, groups on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761/pr-3970/after-thread-on.png) |

- Before: each group shows only the line "Not taken - the planner chooses the entry and the exit of this kind until its slice of #1448 ships".
- After, groups off: each group shows one check box, "First hole stated" or "Last hole stated". The "Not taken" line is gone.
- After, groups on: each group shows its X row, its Y row and its consequence line. The fixture has holes at X -10, 0 and 10. The first group seeds X -10. The last group seeds X 10.
- The images are only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, at `eff3818dd9bf6e57b1a5764387806e6deb015761`, in the folder `pr-3970/`. No image is in this PR branch.
- A temporary headless test rendered the real page code (`pages::properties`, `egui_kittest`, wgpu) at each commit. It used the fixture of the pin `the_hole_kinds_type_their_first_and_last_hole`. The test is not committed.
- The header line "Type: Face" comes from that fixture. The committed operation is a Face and the hole kind is in the draft, because the fixture holds an end mill only.
- Each image is the top 800 px of the 620 x 1400 px render.

## Goldens moved

None moved. `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples/catalog` shows three new files and no changed file:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/hole_order_drill.cl` (new: start C, exit D of four holes)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/hole_order_bore.cl` (new: start B, exit A of four holes)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/hole_order_thread.cl` (new: start the middle hole, exit the first hole of three)

## Not exercised

- The full heavy lanes were not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 107 release steps. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) gives a `P2` PR no heavy step. The light lane ran instead.
- The viewport pick does not snap to a hole yet. Follow-up: #3960. Until then the rows are typed, or MCP sets the picks.
- A posted NC program with picks was not made. The cycle records of the Drill golden (`; CYCLE` lines) are in the picked order, and the post reads those records.
- The first traverse law was not pinned again. It reads the generated path, and the Drill pin asserts that the path starts over the picked first hole.
- A tilted (3+2) Drill with picks was not tested.
- `upstream/main` moved by 18 commits during the gate. `git merge-tree` of this head with the new main is clean. The branch was not refreshed.

## Overlaps

- #3832 (draft) and #3103 (draft, `conflicts`) change the Bore arm of `run_job_arms` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`. They change the destructure list and the `BoreParams` fields. This PR adds one statement before the `bore_started` call. Different lines of the same arm: whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3899 (draft), #3674 and #3251 change other arms of `generate.rs`.

Changelog: Drill, Bore and Thread (mill) take a start point and an exit point as the hole order: the picked hole is cut first or last, and a point that is on no hole is refused by name.

Effort: high

Fixes #3328

title: feat(geometry): import DXF splines and ellipses as tangent arcs
body:
## What changed

- **SPLINE and ELLIPSE import.** Before this change, a DXF drawing with one SPLINE or ELLIPSE stopped the whole import ("unsupported entity"). Now the DXF reader reads them (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/curves.rs`, `nurbs.rs`, `curve_fit.rs`, `biarc.rs`). It lays each curve as tangent-continuous circular arcs (biarcs) and lines. The output is ordinary `Line` and `Arc` primitives, so the chainer, the profile picks and the wire arc contour of #3937 read it with no change.
  - SPLINE: degree 1 to 11, knots, control points, weights (rational), fit-point count. Evaluation is de Boor in homogeneous coordinates.
  - ELLIPSE: centre, major axis, ratio, start and end parameter. A ratio of 1 gives an exact `Circle` or `Arc`.
  - A degree-1 spline gives its control polygon (split at each corner knot).
- **The tolerance and its side.** `CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM` = 0.001 mm, two-sided (Hausdorff). Each fitted piece is checked: each curve point is within 1 µm of the arcs, and each arc point is within 1 µm of the curve. Between the samples, a bound on the curve speed covers the curve side, and the unit speed of the arcs covers the arc side. Speed bound: the derivative control polygon (non-rational spline), `2p (wmax / wmin) D / span` (rational spline), the semi-major axis (ellipse). The output is on no fixed side of the curve. 1 µm is less than half of the wire cover law tolerance (2 µm). An arc with a radius above `CURVE_MAX_RADIUS_MM` (1000 mm) becomes a line, and the same check applies to it.
- **Units.** The bound is in millimetres. A drawing without `$INSUNITS` is read as inches (the largest unit the application lets a caller state), so the bound in drawing units is the tightest. `Document::curve_tolerance` keeps the used value. `SketchData::from_dxf` refuses (`SketchError::CurveTolerance`) when the applied unit makes the bound looser than 1 µm.
- **Refused by name, never clamped.** Degree, knot count, knot order, empty domain, knot multiplicity, weight count, zero / negative / non-finite weights, weight ratio over 1e6, control or fit points in two Z planes (an omitted Z is 0), an orphan or duplicate Z of a control or fit point, counts over the vertex limit (checked before the values are read), fit points without control points, ellipse ratio outside (0, 1], zero axis, zero sweep, parameter over 1e6, tilted axis or extrusion. A curve that needs more evaluations than the drawing budget (50 million) is refused before the work starts. A cusp that 40 halvings cannot fit is refused.
- **INSERT and POINT decision.** They do not stop the import now. Each is skipped and counted in `summary.skipped` (an INSERT with attributes takes its ATTRIB records up to SEQEND). Block expansion is not in this PR; it stays open on #1865. A selected-chain wire cut still refuses a drawing with a skipped INSERT or POINT by name, as for HATCH: the block geometry is not read, so its clearance from the wire cannot be checked.
- **Provenance cleanup (separate small item).** The provenance lines of `crates/post/src/agie/{mod,cutoff,group}.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`, `agie_setup/{cutoff,group,quality,piece}.rs`, `agie_setup/inspection/piece.rs`, `docs/decisions/2966-agie-fine-quality.md`, and the licence section heading in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` and `site/static/icons/LICENSES.txt` no longer name the tool they came from. They say "our own implementation". The MIT licence text stays. The public sources that the lines also name stay. `agie_setup/piece.rs` was added in commit `ae5b858f5` (it was missed before): its provenance line named the tool and a person, and now says "our own implementation of the piece format".
- **Build fix carried.** `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs` on main does not compile (`WireContourOp` has no `start` field, #3952). This branch carries the same hunks as PR #3953 (by mkinney), so the suite builds. When #3953 merges first, the merge is clean.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1865-dxf-spline-ellipse.md`.

## Readings

- Closed cubic SPLINE (fixture `crates/geometry/tests/dxf/spline.dxf`, about 80 mm long): 72 segments, measured Hausdorff 4.1e-4 mm against an independent Cox-de Boor evaluation (bound 1e-3 mm).
- The same spline as a wire die (hole at its centre, generic ISO wire post): 73 `G3` blocks, all laws clean (`verdict.findings` empty, slug captured).
- Unitless rational quarter circle of radius 10: at most 8 arcs, each point within 0.001 / 25.4 of the circle.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-geometry --test dxf`: `curves::closed_cubic_spline_reads_as_tangent_arcs_within_the_bound`, `curves::rational_quarter_circle_spline_becomes_arcs_on_its_circle`, `curves::degree_one_spline_is_its_control_polygon`, `curves::ellipses_read_as_tangent_arcs_and_a_round_one_stays_a_circle`, `curves::a_slender_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_at_its_tight_ends`, `curves::insert_and_point_are_skipped_and_the_rest_reads`.
- `camcraft-geometry --test dxf_refusals`: `curve_refusals::malformed_splines_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_refusals::malformed_ellipses_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_refusals::mutated_curve_records_never_panic` (300 fixed-seed mutations), `curve_refusals::curves_read_for_a_smaller_unit_than_the_applied_one_are_refused`, and the changed `dxf_unsupported_entities_are_refused_by_name` (INSERT now reads).
- `camcraft-app --test wire_dxf_selection`: `arcs::closed_spline_die_cuts_as_tangent_arcs_and_posts_its_golden` (new golden `wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc`), and `arcs::arcs_stay_refused_for_taper_and_a_hatch_still_blocks_the_cut` (now also an INSERT refusal).

## Goldens moved

None. One golden is new: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc`. The six goldens of #3937 and all other goldens are unchanged (the drawings without splines or ellipses read byte for byte as before).

Regenerated after #3988 (merge of main into this branch, commit `1e9840209`): the golden is still added (A) against main. #3988 joins tangent arcs with no zero-length connector. Thus the 72 `G1` blocks that did not move are gone. The 73 `G3` blocks and their I/J centres are unchanged, and the diff has deletions only. Each motion block of the golden now moves the wire (1 `G0`, 2 `G1` for the lead-in and the lead-out, 73 `G3`).

## Not exercised

- No physical cut and no control run of a spline program.
- Sodick and G-EDM goldens for the spline (the arc blocks are the same code path as #3937).
- Splines with only fit points (refused), periodic splines whose control points do not wrap (they read as an open chain), and block expansion.
- The zero-length `G1` after each arc (an output defect of the #3937 arc path) is fixed on main by #3988. The golden was regenerated after that merge and has no such block now.

## Review fixes (review of head `ed5d85de4`)

1. **Coordinate completeness (blocking).** Fixed by the reviewer in `62b3fdf17`. Each control point is X, Y and at most one Z. An omitted Z is 0. Orphan Z, duplicate Z and points in two Z planes are refused by name. Pinned by `curve_refusals::spline_control_points_use_a_per_point_z_default` and `curve_refusals::spline_control_points_refuse_orphan_and_duplicate_z`.
2. **Equal weights are found once (optional).** `Nurbs::new` sets `uniform` one time. `speed()` reads it and does not scan the weights for each span. 40,000 collinear control points (debug build): 13.8 s before, 0.5 s after. Pinned by `curve_bounds::a_long_non_rational_spline_reads_in_linear_time` (bound 5 s).
3. **Near-round ellipse (optional).** A ratio of exactly 1 is the exact circle, with no recorded tolerance. Below 1, the reader uses the circle only when `radius * (1 - ratio)` is within the tolerance in drawing units, and then records the tolerance. Otherwise it fits arcs. Pinned by `curve_bounds::a_near_round_ellipse_is_a_circle_only_within_the_tolerance` (both sides of the bound, and the review case at radius 1e10 mm).

Both `curve_bounds` tests failed on `62b3fdf17` and pass on `8973feb08`.

4. **Fit point elevation (same finding class as item 1).** Fixed in `1359ef98e`. The fit points (group codes 11/21/31) now follow the control point rule of `62b3fdf17`: each fit point is X, Y and at most one Z, and an omitted Z is 0. A Z before X and Y, a duplicate Z, a Y before X and an X with no Y are refused by name. All fit points and all control points must be in one Z plane, else the SPLINE is refused with "fit points are not in one Z plane". Before this fix, the reader ignored group codes 21 and 31, so a fit Z off the plane was not checked. Pinned by `curve_refusals::spline_fit_points_use_a_per_point_z_default` (a fit-only spline with one explicit Z of 1 and one omitted Z, in both orders; all omitted reads at 0; all equal explicit reads at 2; a mixed fit Z and a fit plane that differs from the control plane are refused) and `curve_refusals::spline_fit_points_refuse_orphan_and_duplicate_z`. Both tests failed on `8973feb08` and pass on `1359ef98e`.

On head `ae5b858f5` (merge of main `d80dc6944`, regenerated spline golden, piece provenance line):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1212 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 31.9 min. The log names head `ae5b858f585a16aae26de0ab027fd4b14d603335`. The plan holds `wire_dxf_selection`, `example_catalog*`, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, the ui suites and the clippy step.

- Light lane: `cargo xtask gate light --only "motion light" --only "app light"`: 5 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo xtask merge-plan --delta 3958 --reviewed 1359ef98e`: NEW CODE (the merge `641ac0448` with `wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs` resolved by hand, the golden commit `1e9840209`, the provenance commit `ae5b858f5`).

Heavy: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches 106 steps (geometry is shared). This issue is `P4`, not `P1`, so no heavy step runs ("Heavy lanes at review").

## Review fix

- SPLINE import checks each control point when the next point starts or the record ends. An omitted Z is zero for that point. The reader rejects an orphan or duplicate Z and rejects points in different Z planes.
- `spline_control_points_use_a_per_point_z_default` covers a missing Z in both orders. It also covers zero and equal explicit elevations. `spline_control_points_refuse_orphan_and_duplicate_z` covers orphan, out-of-order and duplicate Z fields.
- Pin proof. Both tests failed on `ed5d85de4` with the new tests and the old parser. Both passed with the fix. `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf --test dxf_refusals` passed all 44 tests.

### Gates on `62b3fdf174b4c02278ce03fa1c2e5d4ee33c7e25`

title: feat(ui): add, move and remove the axes of a machine in the file editor
body:
The Machines pane's file editor gets an "Axis chain" group. The group adds, moves and removes the axis parts of a `.mch` file, reverses a linear axis, and sets the direction of a rotary axis. The editor changes the file's own JSON, so it keeps every key that it does not know. The decisions and the open questions are in `docs/decisions/2756-machine-axis-chain.md`.

**Before** (v0.26.0): the file editor of the same grblHAL 3-axis machine, with no Axis chain group above General.

![Before: the Machines file editor in v0.26.0, General first and no Axis chain group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2756/axis-chain-before.png)

**After** (this PR): the Axis chain group above General.

![After: the Axis chain group on the same 3-axis mill, above General](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2756/axis-chain.png)

## What changed

- **`MachineDraft`** (`crates/app/src/machine/chain.rs`, `draft.rs`) adds, moves and removes axis parts in `kinematics.default.parts`, like `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant`. A refused edit changes nothing. The validator judges the result as before.
  - A new axis goes **on the table** (beside the table's axes, before the head; a rotary there turns the work) or **carries the head** (it takes the head's slot; a rotary there tilts the tool).
  - **Remove** keeps what the axis carried: its `parts` take its place, in order. Its controller row goes with it.
  - **Up and Down** trade an axis with its neighbour row. The tree keeps its shape, so a move never changes which slot carries the head. An axis keeps all its own keys (`pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, `sign_convention`, unknown keys) and gets the `parent` and `chain_order` (#1962) of its new slot.
  - A move trades only with an axis of the same kind (rotary or linear) that moves the same thing (the work or the tool). Other moves are refused, and the refusal says to remove the axis and add it again.
  - A linear is reversed with `"direction": -1` (#373). Back to standard removes the key.
  - A rotary's `axis` is ±X, ±Y, ±Z or three numbers. The editor suggests the RS-274 letter (about X is A, about Y is B, about Z is C) and adds a note to a row whose letter does not agree. It does not refuse it.
- **The validator** keys the work-length refusals by axis and key (`A nose_to_axis`, `work_length_refusals` in `crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs`), so each refusal shows at its row and not above the grid. The rule is the parser's own rule.
- **The editor rows** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/machine_axis_chain.rs`) draw in one property grid, like General and the editor's other groups (`prop_grid` in `layout/form.rs`, #1122): one setting per row, the label in the first column and the control beside it, help as a hover text. A first version pushed the controls to the right edge (`prop_row`), so in a wide pane they drifted away from their labels. Each axis has a row with its letter and kind and the buttons Up, Down and ✖. Their accessible names are "Move A up", "Move A down" and "Remove A". The direction and the place of a new axis are dropdowns.
  - `nose_to_axis` (#804) and `axis_to_table` (#1107) are rows for a rotary that turns the work. A rotary that carries the head shows them only when the file states one, so that the user can clear it.
  - A row whose `offset` has no parent rotary gets a note (see Q1 below).
  - The fields have stable ids, so a note or a refusal that comes or goes above a field does not take the focus while the user types.
- **The rows are built once per edit** (the frame-cost rule, #2238). `MachineDraft::chain_view` (`crates/app/src/machine/chain_view.rs`) holds the rows, each row's notes and the refusal keys that show at a row. The draft is the file's one writer: `value` is now private, read with `value()`, and every write, `value_mut()` included, drops the view. A still frame reads it back. The group and the view are named `ui/machines.editor.axis_chain` and `ui/machines.editor.axis_chain.view` for the frame probe. The draft's `refusals()` and `groups()` still run on each frame, as on `main` before this PR. Five existing test lines read `value()` instead of the field.
- The Machines pane's editor and detail view fill the width of the pane.

The machine window ("edit a machine" from the Setup pane) also has "add axis". That window edits the mounted `Machine` (a flat list of axes and limits) through `EditMachineApply`. This group edits the axis tree of the `.mch` file and keeps the keys that the editor does not know. They are two different tools, and this PR does not change the machine window.

## Open questions (the decision file takes the recommended option)

The maintainer has not answered these yet. Each one has a cost to change in the decision file.

- **Q1** (comment of 2026-11-20): an `offset` on a rotary with no parent rotary. This PR shows a note at the row and does not refuse the file. We recommend a refusal in the validator.
- **Q2** (comment of 2026-11-20): a move trades only with an axis of the same kind. This PR also refuses a trade between an axis that moves the work and one that moves the tool.
- The three questions in the issue: the order with #1970, the #785 pair beside the #1962 pair, and a machine with a tilting head and a rotary table. This PR adds a head axis and a table axis to the same file, but does not draw a "Kinematics" group.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the tree of `e1ac7b786` (run just before the commit, nothing else changed): 124 steps, 0 failed, 6.6 min.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` on `e1ac7b786`: 4 steps, 0 failed, 5.3 min.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The gate's batch plan, run one step at a time, on `303188d61` (before the last merge of main): 1,073 steps. One red step was `a_kind_that_is_not_a_kind_refuses_at_the_door`, which main has since fixed ("router" is now a kind). The suite `machine` is green after the merge.
- No heavy step: the issue is `P6`, not `P1` under the safety floor.

## Pinning tests

34 new tests, none removed. The new app tests are modules of the existing `machine` suite (`crates/app/tests/machine/`), so this PR adds no test binary (#3187).

- `crates/app/tests/machine/axis_chain.rs` (15): add on the table and with the head, remove, move, the refusals, unknown keys kept, and `a_rotary_that_turns_the_work_never_trades_with_one_that_tilts_the_tool`.
- `crates/app/tests/machine/axis_rows.rs` (9): what each row says, the RS-274 letter note, the offset note, reverse, turn about, and the work lengths.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_axis_chain.rs` (7): the group through AccessKit labels: an A added on the table, moved and saved; a refused letter and a remove; X reversed and set back; a turn about Y that suggests B and a note for an A about Y; the FlexiHAL router built from a blank mill and saved; the offset note; and a field that keeps its focus when a refusal goes away.
- `crates/app/src/machine/chain_view.rs` (2): a read with no write between builds nothing; every write (add, move, turn, reverse, remove, a hand write through `value_mut`, a field elsewhere) gives the view a fresh build gives.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/frame_cost_caches.rs` (1): `the_axis_chain_is_built_once_per_edit_of_the_machine_file`. Still frames and typing in the form build nothing (the `chain_view_builds` counter); an added axis and a write to the JSON build it again, equal to a fresh build.
- Mutation probes on the cache, each restored after: a `clear` that drops nothing fails `every_write_gives_the_view_a_fresh_build_gives`, the cache test and `an_offset_with_no_parent_rotary_shows_a_note_at_its_row`; a memo that builds on every read fails `a_read_with_no_write_between_builds_nothing` and the cache test.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_edit.rs`: `pick_kind` scrolls the dropdown into view first, because the group makes the form taller.

## Not exercised

- The offset-note UI test was written after the note, so it was not seen red first.
- No output was posted from a machine file that this editor wrote. The values feed the clearance gates and the post kinematics through `parse_mch`, which the app tests check.
- The "Kinematics" group (`pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, `controller.rtcp` as fields) is #1970's. This PR keeps those keys on every edit and does not draw them.
- `validate.rs`, `egui_app/mod.rs`, `egui_app/tests.rs` and `tests/machine.rs` are over 400 lines on main. This PR adds 1, 1, 1 and 9 lines to them.

Changelog: The Machines file editor adds, moves and removes the axes of a machine, reverses a linear axis and sets a rotary's direction.

Fixes #2756

title: fix(mcp): require mutual token proof and line limits on UI link
body:
## What changed

The UI link on Windows and all other platforms verifies that the listening window owns the token before the CLI sends any tool calls:

1. `crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs`:
   - Add `token_proof(token, nonce, role)` with pure-Rust SipHash-2-4 to prove token ownership without sending the raw token over the socket.
   - Update `hello_line`, `hello_matches`, and `hello_ok` for mutual verification.
   - Add zero new dependencies and zero `unsafe` code.
2. `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`:
   - Return the server proof in the hello answer after `hello_matches` succeeds.
3. `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs`:
   - `open` creates a fresh nonce, checks the server proof in constant time, and refuses peers that fail to prove the token.
   - `read_answer_line` reads at most `MAX_ANSWER_LINE + 1` bytes (16 MiB limit) and returns `ReadLineError::TooLong` when a line exceeds the limit.
4. `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`:
   - Add `false_server_on_stale_entry_is_refused_with_no_tool_calls_sent`.

## Decisions

Recorded in `docs/decisions/3874-windows-stale-link.md`.

## Verification

- `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-app --lib mcp::link_client`: 3 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live`: 22 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, 0 warnings

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft_app::mcp::link_client::tests::read_answer_line_accepts_valid_line`
- `camcraft_app::mcp::link_client::tests::read_answer_line_rejects_oversized_line`
- `camcraft_app::mcp::link_client::tests::read_answer_line_rejects_oversized_line_without_newline`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::false_server_on_stale_entry_is_refused_with_no_tool_calls_sent`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::the_link_folder_is_the_users_own`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::the_link_file_follows_the_open_project`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::a_wrong_token_is_refused_and_the_window_goes_on_serving`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::bad_ui_arguments_are_usage_errors`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::a_cli_call_with_no_window_says_so_and_exits_3`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::an_unauthenticated_client_holding_the_link_times_out_and_releases_it`
- `mcp_live::ui_link::a_second_ui_call_during_a_slow_call_reports_busy_and_exits_4`

## Not exercised

- Full workspace batch and release heavy lanes (only `camcraft-app` link code changed).
- Linux and macOS runtime execution (verified locally on Windows; pure-Rust code uses no platform FFI).

title: feat(bore): enter a Bore by plunge, ramp or helix, capped by the approach angles
body:
What changed:
- `OpParams::Bore` has an `entry` field (plunge, ramp, helix). Plunge is the default and is
  not written to the project file.
- The links' approach `ramp_angle` and `helix_angle` cap every descent.

- Arc is refused by name at the command doors: `OpParams::bore_entry_refusal` is one allow-list (plunge, ramp, helix). `CreateOperation`, `EditOperationParams` and paste call it through `named_refusal`. The generator keeps the same check as a second check.

title: feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal
body:
feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal

## What changed

Issue #2772, parts 1 and 2 of the plan in
`docs/decisions/2772-rotary-4axis-refusal.md`. The rotary kinds
(Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) read their rotation
axis from a STATEMENT first; today's free fit is the fallback, and
nothing stated keeps every behaviour bit for bit.

1. The stated-axis resolver, `camcraft_app::rotary_stated` over
   `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_stated`:
   - the op's own `stated_axis` direction first, else the mounted
     machine's stated rotary lines (a stated `axis` vector, else the
     RS-274 letter's line - the index-swing clause's own
     `rotary_line` reading, so one law reads both doors);
   - each line anchored through the setup's work offset origin (the
     indexed post's setup law: the WCS sits on the rotary
     centreline), canonicalized the fit's own way (signed, pinned to
     the `o . u = 0` foot), so a part truly on the line keeps the
     fitted path move for move;
   - JUDGED, never trusted: the fit's own concurrency share,
     coarseness skip and bearing law about the stated line
     (`axis_stated::judged_any`). A disagreement refuses by name:
     the part's own fitted axis and the two acts that fix it when
     the model is a revolve placed off the line; the freeform's
     4-axis wording (with the pinned "share no rotation axis"
     words) when no axis fits at all. Never a silent fall back to a
     free fit when a line was stated. A stated line that leans or is
     no direction refuses by name, as the swing clause does.
2. The caller switch, stated first / fit fallback:
   - `fixture::rotary_axis_of` - feeds the sim's chord pass
     (`stock_sim_rotary::rotary_plan`), the first traverse and the
     post gate's struck-steel law (`fixture_struck`): all three
     follow with no change of their own;
   - `first_traverse::turned_axis` - already prefers the job axis,
     which is now the stated-or-fitted line;
   - `rotary_law::rotary_into` - the radial field verdict takes the
     job's resolved axis (`rotary_axis`), keeping its fail-closed
     Gouge for the nothing-known case;
   - `rotary_picks::usable` and the centre-cutting audit's
     `revolved_bar_stated` - judge and read the resolved axis;
   - the letter door `rotary_gate::letter_gate` (moved from
     generate.rs) - a stated line answers the letter without a fit,
     held to the machine inventory;
   - the three motion kernels grow `*_stated` entries
     (`rotary_contour_stated`, `rotary_parallel_over_stated`,
     `rotary_offset_stated`) that take the judged axis; the plain
     entries keep the fit inside, so turning, drilling and every
     existing golden path are untouched.
3. The op param: `stated_axis` on the three arms - a direction
   ratio, never unit-scaled (the machine file's own law for its
   `axis` vector), through the WCS origin, overriding the machine
   line. UI edit (the rotary page's Passes tab, an armed group of
   three direction numbers riding the existing EditOperationParams
   commit), MCP patch (`edit_operation`'s merge patch over the DTO,
   automatic), project round-trip (`stated_axis`, PROJECT_VERSION
   steps to v81 - BREAKING, an incompatible project-format change.
   v78 is upstream's own step (eserved_tools, #2604), v79 its
   conditional tip form (#3368) and v80 the minimum_cone_radius step
   (#3153); a v78 or v79 reader accepts this branch's old v78 and
   drops the stated key on re-save. v81 is the next correctly-ordered
   free version: an older reader refuses the file rather than drop
   the statement and turn the part about an axis the user never
   named. A v78, v79 and v80 file still open - the v79 keys read
   natively, pinned by the round-trip test).
4. The cache stamp: the op's own direction, the machine's stated
   lines and the WCS anchor enter the digest ONLY when a line is
   stated - no cached path of a document without one goes stale.

## The readings

- The WCS origin is the stated line's anchor: the post subtracts the
  work offset from world coordinates, so in program coordinates the
  rotary centreline passes through the WCS origin - the same law the
  index-swing clause and the lathe spindle law read.
- The judge is the fit's own (`axis.rs`'s `data_of` + `judge`): the
  tolerance, the 90% concurrency share, the coarseness skip and the
  bearing law, evaluated about the stated line instead of a candidate
  from the eigen search. On the reporter's helical rotor the judge
  fails and the radial raster stays LOCKED (the decision doc's law:
  its radial pose can gouge on helical lobes) - the disagreement
  refusal says so and names the 4-axis case.
- A machine whose work-turning rotary states no `axis` vector keeps
  today's fit (absent is not stated, never zero). A trunnion's
  work-turning pair is read in chain order and the first line the
  model holds wins, so a standing revolve takes the C and a lying
  one takes the A.

## Pinning tests

- motion `axis_stated_tests`: a revolve holds its stated line and
  reads the fitted axis bit for bit; the canonical line is signed
  and pinned; a stated line away from the part names the part's own
  axis; the helical screw refuses with the 4-axis wording; an empty
  mesh refuses like the fit.
- app `rotary_stated_axis`:
  `a_stated_machine_line_generates_the_fitted_path` (microARC 4 +
  laid revolve: move-for-move the fitted program),
  `the_millturns_stated_c_carries_the_standing_bar` (C answered
  without a fit, the stamp runs),
  `the_screw_rotor_on_a_stated_A_is_refused_by_name` (the radial
  kinds stay locked on the screw),
  `the_screw_rotor_without_a_stated_line_keeps_the_old_refusal`
  (the pinned "share no rotation axis" words untouched),
  `a_stated_line_away_from_the_part_names_the_parts_own_axis` (both
  the disagreement and the letter-door wordings),
  `a_stated_line_the_part_holds_on_a_machine_that_has_it_generates`
  (the op's own statement, either sign),
  `a_work_offset_move_moves_the_stated_line_and_refuses` (the
  anchor is the WCS's own position),
  `a_stated_axis_round_trips_the_project_file` (v81 round-trip, v77 steps up unstated),
  `a_v77_file_opens_and_a_newer_file_is_refused` (the version pin),
  `a_stated_axis_on_every_rotary_kind_needs_the_new_reader` (the
  old-reader boundary, one op of each rotary kind),
  `a_common_translation_does_not_defeat_the_stated_line_judge` (the
  review's mutation: the model and stock at Y+10000, clearance 100 -
  the work offset on the part generates, 1 mm and 2 mm off refuse by
  name).
- motion `axis_stated_tests`, the translation pins: a part moved with
  its line holds it on every coordinate axis and reads the fit's own
  axis; a wrong line 1 mm off on each of the three coordinate planes
  refuses at home and after every common translation.
- app `project_roundtrip`:
  `a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_project_version` (the ladder
  stepped past v79: a tip-form file writes v81, and a v79 file - the
  tip-form era's own - still opens and reads its tips whole).
- ui `egui_app::tests::rotary_stated_axis` (new, the review's item):
  the group's labels, roles and enabled state, the Apply commit and
  one undo, across the three rotary kinds
  (`the_stated_axis_group_arms_edits_and_undoes_on_every_rotary_kind`);
  the help text follows the resolver's order - the machine's stated
  line first, the fit only when nothing is stated
  (`the_help_text_follows_the_resolver_machine_line_first`).
- Test placement: `crates/app/tests/rotary_stated_axis.rs` stays a
  top-level binary because no existing directory suite covers the
  rotary domain - its siblings (`rotary_verify.rs`,
  `rotary_letter.rs`, `rotary_contour_x.rs`) are all top-level - and
  its gate map spans app::rotary_stated, app::operation, app::project
  and the motion judge.
- app `rotary_gate`: `a_stated_line_answers_the_letter_without_a_fit`
  (the screw's fit refuses, the stated line still answers).
- app `rotary_field_parity`:
  `the_stated_axis_parallel_reads_the_radial_law` - the heavy-lane
  parity of the stated-A program (the field eye vs the radial law,
  `#[ignore]`d like its three siblings; the quick suite pins the
  path equality, this lane proves the stated axis flows the whole
  sim pipeline at the verdict class).
- The continuous 4-axis example regenerated at v81 (its op follows
  the microARC's stated line - the same path the fit reads).

## What was NOT exercised

- The heavy parity lane runs at a cut, not here (the quick gate
  pins the path equality instead).
- No UI pixel snapshot is touched (release-lane only).

## Screenshots

Before and after of the Passes tab's stated-axis controls (the
fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, captured through the
egui_kittest properties-page harness - no pixels enter this branch):

- [before](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-before.png) -
  the pre-change Passes tab, no stated-axis group
- [after, unstated](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-after-unstated.png) -
  the group sits above the passes, disarmed
- [after, stated](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-passes-after-stated.png) -
  armed, the three direction rows seeded with X
- [after, the offset kind](https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr3674-rotary-offset-after-stated.png) -
  the same group on Rotary Offset's Passes tab

## Not included (the issue stays open)

- The RADIAL DROP FINISH KERNEL and the radial-step roughing
  (decision part 3/4): the live claim on
  `mkinney:issue/2772-radial-drop` holds that work. This PR's
  disagreement refusal keeps the radial kinds locked on helical
  parts until that kernel can consume the stated axis safely.
- No 360-degree radial drop finish for Rotary Parallel, no
  Doosan/Fanuc posting of one - same slice.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read a
stated rotation axis first (the operation's own direction, else the
machine's stated rotary line through the work offset origin), judged
against the model's faces - a part on the stated line cuts the fitted
path unchanged, a part whose faces disagree refuses by name (the
4-axis case named), and nothing stated keeps the fitted axis (v81 project files - a breaking project-format change).
